# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `bun run docs` from src/registry.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every `tenantctl` command (225), grouped by area. `tenantctl <area> <command> --help` shows the same detail, and `tenantctl tools --json` gives it as JSON Schema for agents.

Risk: **read** changes nothing; **write** needs writes enabled; **destructive** also needs a person to approve the preview (OS dialog or terminal prompt; a `--confirm` token in `token` mode).

## Index

**troubleshoot**: One-shot diagnostics: a user, a device, sign-in failures, mail delivery

| Command                                                 | What it does                                                                                                     | Risk |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---- |
| [`troubleshoot user`](#tenantctl-troubleshoot-user)     | Everything that can stop a user working: account, licenses, MFA, risk, sign-in failures, devices, mailbox        | read |
| [`troubleshoot signin`](#tenantctl-troubleshoot-signin) | Why a user cannot sign in: failures grouped by error code, the Conditional Access policy that blocked them       | read |
| [`troubleshoot device`](#tenantctl-troubleshoot-device) | Why a device is non-compliant, blocked or misbehaving: compliance, sync, Entra state, profiles, sign-ins         | read |
| [`troubleshoot mail`](#tenantctl-troubleshoot-mail)     | Why an email did not arrive: message trace, delivery events for failures, recipient inbox rules                  | read |
| [`troubleshoot tenant`](#tenantctl-troubleshoot-tenant) | Tenant health check: Microsoft outages, directory sync, licenses, expiring app secrets, devices, risk, incidents | read |

**entra**: Users, guests, groups, licenses, sign-ins, MFA, roles, apps and consent, Conditional Access, risk, reviews

| Command                                                                                     | What it does                                                                                  | Risk        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| [`entra users list`](#tenantctl-entra-users-list)                                           | List or search users, with filters for disabled, guest, unlicensed and inactive accounts      | read        |
| [`entra users get`](#tenantctl-entra-users-get)                                             | Show a user: account state, sync source, manager, licenses, password age and last sign-in     | read        |
| [`entra users groups`](#tenantctl-entra-users-groups)                                       | List a user's groups (including nested) and directory roles                                   | read        |
| [`entra users licenses`](#tenantctl-entra-users-licenses)                                   | Explain a user's licenses: direct vs group-assigned, errors, and disabled service plans       | read        |
| [`entra users auth-methods`](#tenantctl-entra-users-auth-methods)                           | Show a user's MFA/sign-in methods and registration status                                     | read        |
| [`entra users devices`](#tenantctl-entra-users-devices)                                     | List the Entra device objects a user owns or registered                                       | read        |
| [`entra users signins`](#tenantctl-entra-users-signins)                                     | Show a user's recent sign-ins with failures explained                                         | read        |
| [`entra users create`](#tenantctl-entra-users-create)                                       | Create a cloud user account (returns the temporary password)                                  | write       |
| [`entra users update`](#tenantctl-entra-users-update)                                       | Change a user's profile fields or manager                                                     | write       |
| [`entra users disable`](#tenantctl-entra-users-disable)                                     | Block a user from signing in (accountEnabled = false)                                         | destructive |
| [`entra users enable`](#tenantctl-entra-users-enable)                                       | Allow a disabled user to sign in again (accountEnabled = true)                                | write       |
| [`entra users reset-password`](#tenantctl-entra-users-reset-password)                       | Reset a user's password (returns the temporary password once)                                 | destructive |
| [`entra users revoke-sessions`](#tenantctl-entra-users-revoke-sessions)                     | Sign a user out of every app and device by revoking refresh tokens                            | destructive |
| [`entra users delete`](#tenantctl-entra-users-delete)                                       | Delete a user (soft delete: restorable for 30 days)                                           | destructive |
| [`entra users deleted`](#tenantctl-entra-users-deleted)                                     | List deleted users that can still be restored                                                 | read        |
| [`entra users restore`](#tenantctl-entra-users-restore)                                     | Restore a deleted user (within 30 days of deletion)                                           | write       |
| [`entra users license add`](#tenantctl-entra-users-license-add)                             | Assign a license SKU to a user, optionally with some service plans disabled                   | write       |
| [`entra users license remove`](#tenantctl-entra-users-license-remove)                       | Remove a directly assigned license SKU from a user                                            | destructive |
| [`entra users tap`](#tenantctl-entra-users-tap)                                             | Issue a Temporary Access Pass so a user can sign in and register MFA                          | destructive |
| [`entra users auth-method remove`](#tenantctl-entra-users-auth-method-remove)               | Remove one MFA/sign-in method from a user (e.g. an old phone)                                 | destructive |

| [`entra users bulk-create`](#tenantctl-entra-users-bulk-create)                             | Create many cloud users from a CSV, with manager, license and groups per row                  | write       |
| [`entra groups add-members`](#tenantctl-entra-groups-add-members)                           | Add every member listed in a CSV column to a group, reporting each row                        | write       |
| [`entra tenant`](#tenantctl-entra-tenant)                                                   | Tenant overview: name, id, domains (managed/federated) and directory sync health              | read        |
| [`entra groups list`](#tenantctl-entra-groups-list)                                         | List or search groups, with derived type (security/m365/distribution) and Teams flag          | read        |

| [`entra groups remove-member`](#tenantctl-entra-groups-remove-member)                       | Remove a user, device or group from a group                                                   | destructive |
| [`entra groups create`](#tenantctl-entra-groups-create)                                     | Create a security or Microsoft 365 group, optionally with an owner and members                | write       |
| [`entra licenses`](#tenantctl-entra-licenses)                                               | Tenant license inventory: purchased, assigned and available per SKU                           | read        |
| [`entra signins`](#tenantctl-entra-signins)                                                 | Search tenant-wide sign-in logs by user, app, IP, error code or country                       | read        |
| [`entra signin-error`](#tenantctl-entra-signin-error)                                       | Explain an Entra sign-in error code (AADSTS...) and what to do about it                       | read        |

| [`entra apps expiring`](#tenantctl-entra-apps-expiring)                                     | App registrations whose client secrets or certificates expire soon or already expired         | read        |
| [`entra ca list`](#tenantctl-entra-ca-list)                                                 | List Conditional Access policies with a one-line summary of who, what and how                 | read        |
| [`entra ca get`](#tenantctl-entra-ca-get)                                                   | Show one Conditional Access policy with users, groups, roles, apps and locations named        | read        |
| [`entra risky-users`](#tenantctl-entra-risky-users)                                         | Users Entra ID Protection flags as risky (leaked credentials, impossible travel...)           | read        |
| [`entra risky-users dismiss`](#tenantctl-entra-risky-users-dismiss)                         | Dismiss a user's risk after confirming it was a false positive                                | write       |
| [`entra risky-users confirm-compromised`](#tenantctl-entra-risky-users-confirm-compromised) | Mark a user as confirmed compromised (raises user risk to high)                               | destructive |

| [`entra devices get`](#tenantctl-entra-devices-get)                                         | Show an Entra device with its registered owners and users                                     | read        |
| [`entra devices disable`](#tenantctl-entra-devices-disable)                                 | Disable an Entra device so it can no longer authenticate (lost or stolen device)              | destructive |
| [`entra devices enable`](#tenantctl-entra-devices-enable)                                   | Re-enable a disabled Entra device                                                             | write       |

| [`entra apps revoke-consent`](#tenantctl-entra-apps-revoke-consent)                         | Revoke delegated grants and/or application permissions from an app (illicit consent response) | destructive |

| [`entra apps enable`](#tenantctl-entra-apps-enable)                                         | Re-enable a disabled enterprise app                                                           | write       |

## troubleshoot

One-shot diagnostics: a user, a device, sign-in failures, mail delivery

### `tenantctl troubleshoot user`

Everything that can stop a user working: account, licenses, MFA, risk, sign-in failures, devices, mailbox

Start here for any "X can't sign in / get email / use Teams" request. Checks run in parallel and each degrades on its own: `unavailable` lists sections that could not be checked (usually a missing permission or licence, e.g. sign-in logs need Entra ID P1, risk needs P2, another user's mailbox needs app-only auth, mailbox-level forwarding needs `tenantctl auth login --service exchange` and pwsh). `findings` is ranked high > medium > low > info, each with the command to investigate or fix it; `verdict` is a one-line answer to relay to the user. Sign-in failures are grouped by error code and marked "still failing" when no successful sign-in followed them. Mailbox forwarding (inbox rules and the mailbox-level setting) outside the company is flagged high: it is the usual persistence trick after an account takeover.

```
tenantctl troubleshoot user <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--days`            | number | Sign-in history to analyze, in days (max 30). (default `7`)   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl troubleshoot user jane@contoso.com
tenantctl troubleshoot user "Jane Doe" --days 14
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLog.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`, `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All`; application `AuditLog.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`, `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All`; Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Global Reader or Security Reader or Helpdesk Administrator

### `tenantctl troubleshoot signin`

Why a user cannot sign in: failures grouped by error code, the Conditional Access policy that blocked them

Deeper than `troubleshoot user` for sign-in problems. Each failure group carries the error explained, the apps/IPs/locations/devices involved, the Conditional Access policies whose result was "failure" with the controls they required (MFA, compliant device...), and the latest correlation id for a Microsoft support case. `latest` is the most recent attempt; compare `lastSuccess` to tell "still failing" from "fixed". Requires Entra ID P1 for sign-in logs.

```
tenantctl troubleshoot signin <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required)              |
| `--days`            | number | Sign-in history to analyze, in days (max 30). (default `7`)                |
| `--app`             | string | Only sign-ins to apps whose name starts with this, e.g. "Microsoft Teams". |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl troubleshoot signin jane@contoso.com
tenantctl troubleshoot signin jane --app Outlook --days 2
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLog.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All`; application `AuditLog.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All`; role Reports Reader or Security Reader or Global Reader

### `tenantctl troubleshoot device`

Why a device is non-compliant, blocked or misbehaving: compliance, sync, Entra state, profiles, sign-ins

Start here for "my laptop/phone can't access email/Teams", "device not compliant" or "is this device healthy". Accepts a device name, serial number, Intune device id or Entra device id. Combines Intune compliance (with the failing settings in one sentence), last check-in, the Entra ID device object (disabled, missing, compliance not yet reported), configuration profile errors, encryption, storage, pending remote actions, and the primary user's failed sign-ins from this device. `findings` is ranked, each with a next command; `unavailable` lists what could not be checked.

```
tenantctl troubleshoot device <device> [options]
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name, serial number or id. (required)                     |
| `--days`                | number | Sign-in history to check for this device, in days. (default `7`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl troubleshoot device LAPTOP-0042
tenantctl troubleshoot device C02XK1ABJHD5
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLog.Read.All`, `Device.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `AuditLog.Read.All`, `Device.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl troubleshoot mail`

Why an email did not arrive: message trace, delivery events for failures, recipient inbox rules

Start here for "I didn't get the email from X". Traces messages to the recipient (optionally from a sender or with a subject), pulls the delivery events for up to 5 undelivered ones (failed, quarantined, junked, pending) so the last event explains the outcome, and checks the recipient's inbox rules that delete, move or forward mail. Message trace covers the last 10 days per query (90 days back) and needs the one-time message-trace service principal (see `tenantctl exchange trace --help`); inbox rules of another user need app-only auth.

```
tenantctl troubleshoot mail <recipient> [options]
```

| Argument                      | Type   | Description                                            |
| ----------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<recipient>` / `--recipient` | string | Recipient email address. (required)                    |
| `--sender`                    | string | Sender email address.                                  |
| `--subject`                   | string | Text the subject contains.                             |
| `--days`                      | number | How far back to trace, in days (max 10). (default `2`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl troubleshoot mail jane@contoso.com --sender billing@vendor.com
tenantctl troubleshoot mail jane@contoso.com --subject "Invoice" --days 5
```

Permissions: delegated `Domain.Read.All`, `ExchangeMessageTrace.Read.All`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`; application `Domain.Read.All`, `ExchangeMessageTrace.Read.All`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`; role Exchange Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl troubleshoot tenant`

Tenant health check: Microsoft outages, directory sync, licenses, expiring app secrets, devices, risk, incidents

Use for "is something wrong with our Microsoft 365?", "why are several users affected?", or a daily/weekly admin check. Each area is checked in parallel and degrades independently; `unavailable` lists what could not be checked (e.g. risk needs Entra ID P2, incidents need Defender XDR). `findings` is ranked with the command to drill into each.

```
tenantctl troubleshoot tenant
```

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl troubleshoot tenant
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `SecurityEvents.Read.All`, `SecurityIncident.Read.All`, `ServiceHealth.Read.All`, `User.Read`; application `Application.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `Organization.Read.All`, `SecurityEvents.Read.All`, `SecurityIncident.Read.All`, `ServiceHealth.Read.All`; role Global Reader

## entra

Users, guests, groups, licenses, sign-ins, MFA, roles, apps and consent, Conditional Access, risk, reviews

### `tenantctl entra users list`

List or search users, with filters for disabled, guest, unlicensed and inactive accounts

Use to find users or answer "who is disabled / unlicensed / a guest / inactive". Filters combine with AND. --search matches display name, UPN and mail. --inactive-days N returns users whose last interactive sign-in is older than N days and adds lastSignIn; it needs AuditLog.Read.All and Entra ID P1/P2, cannot be combined with other filters (Graph limitation), and omits users who have never signed in. Follow up with `tenantctl entra users get <upn>` for one user.

```
tenantctl entra users list [options]
```

| Argument          | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--search`        | string  | Match display name, UPN or mail (word prefix).               |
| `--department`    | string  | Exact department name.                                       |
| `--disabled`      | boolean | Only accounts with sign-in blocked.                          |
| `--guests`        | boolean | Only guest (B2B) accounts.                                   |
| `--unlicensed`    | boolean | Only users with no license assigned.                         |
| `--inactive-days` | number  | Only users with no interactive sign-in for N days.           |
| `--top`           | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`           | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users list --search jane
tenantctl entra users list --department Sales --disabled
tenantctl entra users list --unlicensed --all
tenantctl entra users list --inactive-days 90
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`; application `User.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra users get`

Show a user: account state, sync source, manager, licenses, password age and last sign-in

Start here for any question about one person. accountEnabled=false means sign-in is blocked. isSynced=true means the account is mastered in on-premises AD (change it there). daysSinceLastSignIn uses the last successful sign-in and needs AuditLog.Read.All plus Entra ID P1/P2; without them signIns shows an error and the rest still works. Next: `users signins` for failures, `users auth-methods` for MFA, `users licenses` for missing apps.

```
tenantctl entra users get <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users get jane@contoso.com
tenantctl entra users get "Jane Doe"
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`; application `User.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra users groups`

List a user's groups (including nested) and directory roles

Shows every group the user is in directly or through nesting, with type (Security, Microsoft 365, Mail-enabled security, Distribution) and whether membership is dynamic, plus active directory (admin) roles. Use to explain why someone has access to a site/app or receives a policy. Eligible (PIM) roles are not shown.

```
tenantctl entra users groups <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string  | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                     |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users groups jane@contoso.com --all
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `User.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra users licenses`

Explain a user's licenses: direct vs group-assigned, errors, and disabled service plans

Use for "why doesn't X have Teams/Exchange/etc.". Each assignment shows assignedVia (direct or group), state and error (CountViolation = no seats, MutuallyExclusiveViolation = conflicting plans, ...) with an explanation, disabledPlans (service plans switched off in that assignment) and plansNotReady (plans whose provisioning is pending or failed; delegated sign-in only). A missing usageLocation blocks assignment. Fix with `users license add/remove` or by changing group membership.

```
tenantctl entra users licenses <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users licenses jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `User.Read.All`, `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra users auth-methods`

Show a user's MFA/sign-in methods and registration status

Use for MFA problems ("not getting prompts", "new phone"). methods lists each registered method with its id (needed for `users auth-method remove`). registration (needs AuditLog.Read.All, Entra ID P1/P2) shows isMfaRegistered/isMfaCapable, SSPR state, passwordless capability and the default MFA method. hasStrongMethod=false means only password/email: issue a TAP (`users tap`) so they can register. Authentication Administrators see phone numbers masked.

```
tenantctl entra users auth-methods <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users auth-methods jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`; application `User.Read.All`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`; role Authentication Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl entra users devices`

List the Entra device objects a user owns or registered

Entra ID view of the user's devices: join type (Entra joined / Hybrid joined / Entra registered), isCompliant and isManaged (as Conditional Access sees them), last sign-in, and whether the device object is enabled. Use when CA blocks a device. For Intune details (compliance reasons, sync) use the intune commands. Delegated sign-in only (Graph has no application permission for this).

```
tenantctl entra users devices <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users devices jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra users signins`

Show a user's recent sign-ins with failures explained

Use for "X can't sign in". Newest first. Each entry shows app, client, IP, location, device (compliant? joined?), result, errorCode with a plain-language explanation and suggested action, Conditional Access result, whether MFA was required/satisfied and sign-in risk. Interactive and non-interactive (token refresh) sign-ins are both included. Needs AuditLog.Read.All and Entra ID P1/P2; logs are kept 30 days (7 on free).

```
tenantctl entra users signins <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string  | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--days`            | number  | How many days back to look (max 30). (default `7`)            |
| `--failures-only`   | boolean | Only failed sign-ins.                                         |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                     |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users signins jane@contoso.com
tenantctl entra users signins jane@contoso.com --failures-only --days 3
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`; application `User.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`; role Reports Reader or Security Reader or Global Reader

### `tenantctl entra users create`

Create a cloud user account (returns the temporary password) **[write]**

Creates an enabled member account. Without --password a strong random password is generated and returned once as temporaryPassword: hand it to the user securely. The user must change it at first sign-in unless --no-force-change. Set --usage-location now if the user will be licensed, then run `users license add`. The UPN domain must be a verified tenant domain. --manager needs User.ReadWrite.All; if it fails the user is still created and the result says so.

```
tenantctl entra users create --display-name <string> --upn <string> [options]
```

| Argument           | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--display-name`   | string  | Full name shown in the address book. (required)              |
| `--upn`            | string  | Sign-in name, e.g. jane@contoso.com. (required)              |
| `--mail-nickname`  | string  | Mail alias; defaults to the UPN prefix.                      |
| `--password`       | string  | Initial password; generated when omitted.                    |
| `--force-change`   | boolean | Require a password change at first sign-in. (default `true`) |
| `--usage-location` | string  | Two-letter country code (needed for licenses).               |
| `--department`     | string  | Department.                                                  |
| `--job-title`      | string  | Job title.                                                   |
| `--manager`        | string  | Manager (UPN, email, name or id).                            |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users create --display-name "Jane Doe" --upn jane@contoso.com --usage-location US
tenantctl entra users create --display-name "Bob Ray" --upn bob@contoso.com --department Sales --manager jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Create`; application `User.Create`; role User Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users update`

Change a user's profile fields or manager **[write]**

Only the options you pass are changed. Synced (on-premises) users must be edited in AD for most fields. --usage-location is required before licenses can be assigned. Dry run (--dry-run) shows old -> new values.

```
tenantctl entra users update <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--display-name`    | string | New display name.                                             |
| `--job-title`       | string | New job title.                                                |
| `--department`      | string | New department.                                               |
| `--office-location` | string | New office location.                                          |
| `--mobile-phone`    | string | New mobile phone number (profile, not MFA).                   |
| `--usage-location`  | string | Two-letter country code.                                      |
| `--employee-id`     | string | Employee id (max 16 chars).                                   |
| `--manager`         | string | New manager (UPN, email, name or id).                         |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users update jane@contoso.com --job-title "Sales Manager" --department Sales
tenantctl entra users update jane@contoso.com --usage-location GB
tenantctl entra users update jane@contoso.com --manager bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.ReadWrite.All`; application `User.ReadWrite.All`; role User Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users disable`

Block a user from signing in (accountEnabled = false) **[destructive]**

Use for offboarding or a compromised account. Existing sessions keep working until their tokens expire: follow with `users revoke-sessions`. Reversible with `users enable`. Synced users must be disabled in AD.

```
tenantctl entra users disable <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users disable jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.EnableDisableAccount.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `User.EnableDisableAccount.All`, `User.Read.All`; role User Administrator or Authentication Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users enable`

Allow a disabled user to sign in again (accountEnabled = true) **[write]**

Reverses `users disable`. Synced users must be enabled in on-premises AD.

```
tenantctl entra users enable <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users enable jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.EnableDisableAccount.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `User.EnableDisableAccount.All`, `User.Read.All`; role User Administrator or Authentication Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users reset-password`

Reset a user's password (returns the temporary password once) **[destructive]**

Sets a new password; without --password a strong one is generated and returned once as temporaryPassword. The user must change it at next sign-in unless --no-force-change. Which admin can reset whom: Helpdesk Administrator resets non-admins and some readers, User Administrator also other user/helpdesk admins, Privileged Authentication Administrator anyone. App-only use also needs an admin role assigned to the app. Synced users need password writeback; reset them in AD otherwise. Consider `users revoke-sessions` after.

```
tenantctl entra users reset-password <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string  | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--password`        | string  | New password; generated when omitted.                         |
| `--force-change`    | boolean | Require a change at next sign-in. (default `true`)            |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users reset-password jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All`; application `User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All`; role Helpdesk Administrator or User Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users revoke-sessions`

Sign a user out of every app and device by revoking refresh tokens **[destructive]**

Use after disabling a user, a password reset for compromise, or a lost device. Apps re-prompt for sign-in; access tokens already issued may work for up to an hour. Does not block sign-in (use `users disable`).

```
tenantctl entra users revoke-sessions <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users revoke-sessions jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.RevokeSessions.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `User.RevokeSessions.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Helpdesk Administrator or User Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users delete`

Delete a user (soft delete: restorable for 30 days) **[destructive]**

Moves the user to deleted items, frees their licenses and soft-deletes their mailbox/OneDrive with them. Restore within 30 days with `users restore <id>`; after that it is permanent. Synced users must be deleted in AD. For offboarding, disabling first is usually safer.

```
tenantctl entra users delete <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users delete jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `User.ReadWrite.All`; application `User.ReadWrite.All`; role User Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users deleted`

List deleted users that can still be restored

Deleted users stay restorable for 30 days; daysUntilPurge shows how long is left. Restore with `users restore <id>`.

```
tenantctl entra users deleted [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users deleted
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Read.All`; application `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra users restore`

Restore a deleted user (within 30 days of deletion) **[write]**

Accepts the id from `users deleted`, or the display name / original UPN. Licenses, group memberships and mailbox come back with the account. Fails if the UPN or mail has been reused meanwhile.

```
tenantctl entra users restore <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                               |
| ------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Deleted user id, display name or original UPN. (required) |

### `tenantctl entra users license add`

Assign a license SKU to a user, optionally with some service plans disabled **[write]**

SKU by part number (ENTERPRISEPACK, SPE_E3), unique fragment (E3) or skuId; `users licenses` and Graph subscribedSkus show names. --disable-plans takes service plan names or ids (e.g. TEAMS1) to switch off; running it again for an assigned SKU replaces its disabled plans. The user needs a usageLocation first. Dry run shows available seats.


Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users license add jane@contoso.com --sku ENTERPRISEPACK --disable-plans YAMMER_ENTERPRISE,SWAY
```

### `tenantctl entra users license remove`

Remove a directly assigned license SKU from a user **[destructive]**

The user loses the apps and services in that SKU (data such as the mailbox is kept for a grace period). Group-inherited licenses cannot be removed per user: the error names the group to change instead.

```

```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                   |

### `tenantctl entra users tap`

Issue a Temporary Access Pass so a user can sign in and register MFA **[destructive]**

Use when a user lost their phone/MFA method or is new and passwordless. Returns the pass once; it replaces any existing pass. Lifetime 10-43200 minutes (policy limits apply). The TAP authentication method policy must be enabled for the user; isUsable=false with DisabledByPolicy means it is not. Multi-use passes need the policy to allow them.

```
tenantctl entra users tap <user> [options]
```

| Argument             | Type    | Description                                                   |
| -------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user`  | string  | User UPN, email, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--lifetime-minutes` | number  | Validity in minutes (10-43200). (default `60`)                |
| `--one-time`         | boolean | Pass can be used for one sign-in only.                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users tap jane@contoso.com
tenantctl entra users tap jane@contoso.com --lifetime-minutes 480 --one-time
```

Permissions: delegated `UserAuthMethod-TAP.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `UserAuthMethod-TAP.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Authentication Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users auth-method remove`

Remove one MFA/sign-in method from a user (e.g. an old phone) **[destructive]**

Get the method id from `users auth-methods`. Typical "new phone" flow: remove the old Authenticator and phone methods, then `users tap` so they can register again. The password cannot be removed. Removing the default method can fail until it is the user's last of that kind.

```

```

| Argument                      | Type   | Description                                                   |

```sh

```

Permissions: delegated `UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Authentication Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator

### `tenantctl entra users invite`

Invite an external person as a B2B guest (optionally straight into a group) **[write]**

Creates the guest account right away and returns its id, UPN (name_domain#EXT#@tenant) and `inviteRedeemUrl`. The invitation email is sent unless --no-email; then share the redeem URL yourself. `status` PendingAcceptance means the guest has not redeemed yet. Inviting an existing guest re-sends the invitation. Refuses addresses in the tenant's own verified domains (those are internal users). --group adds the guest to a security or Microsoft 365 group; if that fails the guest still exists and the result says so. Fails when external collaboration settings block the domain or restrict who can invite.

```
tenantctl entra users invite <email> [options]
```

| Argument              | Type    | Description                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<email>` / `--email` | string  | Guest's email address. (required)                                               |
| `--name`              | string  | Display name for the guest.                                                     |
| `--message`           | string  | Custom text added to the invitation email.                                      |
| `--no-email`          | boolean | Do not send the invitation email (share inviteRedeemUrl).                       |
| `--redirect-url`      | string  | Where the guest lands after redeeming. (default `https://myapps.microsoft.com`) |
| `--group`             | string  | Group to add the guest to (name, mail or id).                                   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra users invite partner@fabrikam.com --name "Pat Partner" --group "Project X Guests"
tenantctl entra users invite contractor@example.org --no-email
```

Permissions: delegated `User.Invite.All`, `User.Read`, `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`; application `User.Invite.All`, `Organization.Read.All`, `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`; role Guest Inviter

### `tenantctl entra users bulk-create`

Create many cloud users from a CSV, with manager, license and groups per row **[write]**

CSV columns: DisplayName, UserPrincipalName (required); optional MailNickname, Password, UsageLocation, Department, JobTitle, Manager (UPN/name, may be another row in the file), License (SKU part number, e.g. SPE_E3; needs UsageLocation), Groups (semicolon-separated names or ids). Max 500 rows. Always run with --dry-run first: it validates every row (missing fields, duplicate UPNs, existing accounts, unknown SKU, manager or group, seat shortfall) and creates nothing. Rows whose UPN already exists are skipped; rows with errors fail; the rest are created. Generated passwords are returned once per row as temporaryPassword (passwords from the file are never echoed); users must change them at first sign-in. A row whose manager, license or group step fails is still created and lists followUpErrors.

```
tenantctl entra users bulk-create <file>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                      |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------- |
| `<file>` / `--file` | string | Path to the CSV file. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl --dry-run entra users bulk-create new-starters.csv
tenantctl entra users bulk-create new-starters.csv
```

Permissions: delegated `User.ReadWrite.All`, `LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`; application `User.ReadWrite.All`, `LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`; role User Administrator

### `tenantctl entra groups add-members`

Add every member listed in a CSV column to a group, reporting each row **[write]**

Reads --column (default UserPrincipalName) from the CSV; values may be UPNs, emails, names or ids, and user:/group:/device: prefixes work as in `groups add-member`. Adds through Graph $batch (20 per request). Each row is added, alreadyMember or failed (unresolvable or rejected); one bad row never stops the rest. Run with --dry-run first to see unresolved rows. Distribution and mail-enabled security groups are managed in Exchange Online. Max 500 rows.

```
tenantctl entra groups add-members <group> --from-csv <string> [options]
```

| Argument              | Type   | Description                                              |
| --------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<group>` / `--group` | string | Group name, mail address or id. (required)               |
| `--from-csv`          | string | CSV file with one member per row. (required)             |
| `--column`            | string | Column holding the member. (default `UserPrincipalName`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl --dry-run entra groups add-members "Finance Team" --from-csv finance.csv
tenantctl entra groups add-members "Project X" --from-csv people.csv --column Email
```

Permissions: delegated `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Groups Administrator

### `tenantctl entra tenant`

Tenant overview: name, id, domains (managed/federated) and directory sync health

Start here to orient in an unfamiliar tenant. `dirSyncStale` is true when on-premises sync is enabled and the last sync is more than 3 hours old (default cycle is 30 minutes) - check the Entra Connect / Cloud Sync server. Federated domains authenticate at an external IdP (e.g. AD FS), which matters when troubleshooting sign-in.


List or search groups, with derived type (security/m365/distribution) and Teams flag

Use to find a group or survey groups of one kind. `type` is derived: m365 (Microsoft 365 group), security, distribution, mail-security (mail-enabled security; members managed in Exchange). `membership` is dynamic or assigned; dynamic groups show their rule. `isTeam` means the group backs a Microsoft Team. `syncedFromOnPrem` groups must be changed in on-premises AD. | `--all`    | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                      |

```sh
tenantctl entra groups list --type dynamic --all
```

Show a group with owners, member count, group-assigned licenses and dynamic rule state

Use to explain what a group is and what it grants. `licenses` lists SKUs assigned through group-based licensing (Entra ID P1). For dynamic groups, `membershipRuleProcessingState` Paused means membership is frozen. `memberCount` counts direct members. Next: `tenantctl entra groups members <group>`.

List group members (users, devices, nested groups); --transitive flattens nesting

Each item has `type` (user, device, group, servicePrincipal, orgContact). Use --transitive to answer "is this user in the group through a nested group?". Hidden-membership groups also need Member.Read.Hidden.

### `tenantctl entra licenses`

Tenant license inventory: purchased, assigned and available per SKU

Answers "do we have a spare license?". `available` = enabled - consumed. `lowOnLicenses` is true when 2 or fewer, or at most 5%, remain. `warning` units are in the renewal grace period; `suspended` units cannot be assigned. Only SKUs with appliesTo=User can be given to people.

```

```

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra licenses
```

Permissions: delegated `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`; application `LicenseAssignment.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra signins`

Search tenant-wide sign-in logs by user, app, IP, error code or country

Use for "why can't X sign in", password-spray checks ("failures from one IP") or "who signed in from country Y". Defaults to the last day; logs are kept 30 days. Each item explains its error code; run `tenantctl entra signin-error <code>` for detail. Requires Entra ID P1 (free tenants get no sign-in API). Interactive and non-interactive user sign-ins both appear in v1.0 results only as interactive; large windows can time out, so narrow with filters.

```
tenantctl entra signins [options]
```

| Argument          | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--user`          | string  | Only this user (UPN, name or id).                            |
| `--app`           | string  | App id, or start of the app display name.                    |
| `--ip`            | string  | Client IP; end with "." to match a prefix (e.g. 203.0.113.). |
| `--error-code`    | string  | Sign-in error code, e.g. 50126 or AADSTS50126.               |
| `--failures-only` | boolean | Only failed sign-ins.                                        |
| `--country`       | string  | Two-letter country code, e.g. US.                            |
| `--days`          | number  | Look back this many days (max 30). (default `1`)             |
| `--top`           | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`           | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra signins --user jane@contoso.com --failures-only --days 3
tenantctl entra signins --ip 203.0.113.7 --days 7
tenantctl entra signins --error-code 50126 --top 200
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLog.Read.All`; application `AuditLog.Read.All`; role Reports Reader or Security Reader

### `tenantctl entra signin-error`

Explain an Entra sign-in error code (AADSTS...) and what to do about it

Offline lookup, no Graph call. Pass the number from a sign-in log `errorCode` or an AADSTS message. `benign` codes are expected noise (e.g. MFA prompts). Unknown codes return Microsoft's lookup URL. Without a code, lists the whole catalog.

```
tenantctl entra signin-error [code]
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                            |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `<code>` / `--code` | string | Error code, e.g. 50126 or AADSTS50126. |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra signin-error 50126
tenantctl entra signin-error AADSTS53003
tenantctl entra signin-error
```

### `tenantctl entra audit`

Search the Entra directory audit log: who changed what, when

Use for "who reset Jane's password", "who added Bob to Global Admins", "what changed on this app". `initiatedBy` is the admin UPN or app name; `targets` lists changed objects and the property names that changed. --activity is a prefix match on the activity name (e.g. "Add member", "Reset password", "Update user"); --category values include UserManagement, GroupManagement, RoleManagement, ApplicationManagement, Policy, Device. Logs are kept 7 days (free) or 30 days (Entra ID P1/P2).

```
tenantctl entra audit [options]
```

| Argument     | Type    | Description                                                       |
| ------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--days`     | number  | Look back this many days. (default `7`)                           |
| `--user`     | string  | Only changes made by this admin (UPN, name or id).                |
| `--target`   | string  | Only changes to this object: user UPN, object id, or name prefix. |
| `--category` | string  | Audit category, e.g. UserManagement.                              |
| `--activity` | string  | Activity name prefix, e.g. "Reset password".                      |
| `--top`      | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                         |
| `--all`      | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).      |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra audit --target jane@contoso.com --days 14
tenantctl entra audit --category RoleManagement --activity "Add member to role"
tenantctl entra audit --user admin@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLog.Read.All`; application `AuditLog.Read.All`; role Reports Reader or Security Reader

### `tenantctl entra roles list`

Who holds each active Entra admin role (Global Administrator etc.)

Use for admin reviews ("who are our Global Admins?"). Shows active assignments, including PIM roles that are currently activated, grouped by role; PIM eligible-but-inactive assignments are not listed (see `roles user`). Members can be users, groups (role-assignable) or service principals. `scope` appears only when the assignment is limited to an administrative unit or object.

```
tenantctl entra roles list [options]
```

| Argument | Type   | Description                               |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `--role` | string | Only roles whose name contains this text. |

Examples:

