tenantctl entra roles list --role "Global Administrator"
```

Permissions: delegated `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`; application `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`

### `tenantctl entra roles user`

A user's active admin roles and PIM-eligible roles

Use for "is Jane an admin?" or before offboarding an admin. `active` are roles in effect now; `eligible` are PIM roles the user can activate (Entra ID P2). Roles held through a role-assignable group show under eligible with memberType Group, but active group-based roles are listed under the group, not the user. A section shows `{ error }` when that part needs a permission or license the tenant lacks.

```
tenantctl entra roles user <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                      |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra roles user jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`, `RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory`; application `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`, `RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory`

### `tenantctl entra apps list`

List or search enterprise apps (service principals)

Use to find an app by name or survey third-party apps. `isMicrosoftApp` marks Microsoft first-party apps; `publisherVerified` means a verified publisher. `assignmentRequired` false means any user can sign in. Next: `tenantctl entra apps get <app>` for the permissions it holds.

```
tenantctl entra apps list [options]
```

| Argument   | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--search` | string  | Words in the app name.                                       |
| `--top`    | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`    | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra apps list --search zoom
tenantctl entra apps list --all
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.Read.All`; application `Application.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra apps get`

Show an enterprise app with the application and delegated permissions it was granted

Use for consent reviews or "what can this app access?". `applicationPermissions` are app-only roles (e.g. Mail.Read on Microsoft Graph) - powerful because they need no user. `delegatedPermissions` are scopes consented for users: consent "admin" applies to everyone, "user" to one user. Accepts name, appId or object id.

```
tenantctl entra apps get <app>
```

| Argument          | Type   | Description                              |
| ----------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `<app>` / `--app` | string | App name, appId or object id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra apps get "Zoom"
tenantctl entra apps get 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`; application `Application.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra apps expiring`

App registrations whose client secrets or certificates expire soon or already expired

Use to prevent outages from expired secrets ("integration stopped working"). Checks every app registration; `daysLeft` < 0 means already expired. Rotate in the Entra admin center (App registrations > Certificates & secrets), then update the consuming service. SAML signing certificates live on enterprise apps and are not covered.

```
tenantctl entra apps expiring [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--days` | number  | Include credentials expiring within N days. (default `30`)   |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra apps expiring
tenantctl entra apps expiring --days 90
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.Read.All`; application `Application.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra ca list`

List Conditional Access policies with a one-line summary of who, what and how

Use to understand why a sign-in was blocked or MFA was required. `state` report-only policies log but never enforce. Scope fields read like "All", "3 specific" or "GuestsOrExternalUsers + 1 specific"; `grant` is the requirement (e.g. "mfa OR compliantDevice", "block"). Needs Entra ID P1. Next: `tenantctl entra ca get <policy>` to see names of included/excluded users, groups, roles and apps.

```
tenantctl entra ca list [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra ca list
```

Permissions: delegated `Policy.Read.All`; application `Policy.Read.All`; role Security Reader

### `tenantctl entra ca get`

Show one Conditional Access policy with users, groups, roles, apps and locations named

Accepts the policy id or part of its name. `resolved` translates ids in the conditions to names (unresolvable ids stay as ids, e.g. deleted objects). Use with `tenantctl entra signins --user X` to match a failed sign-in (error 53003) to the policy that blocked it.

```
tenantctl entra ca get <policy>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                   |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------- |
| `<policy>` / `--policy` | string | Policy id or name. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra ca get "Require MFA for admins"
```

Permissions: delegated `Policy.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`; application `Policy.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`; role Security Reader

### `tenantctl entra risky-users`

Users Entra ID Protection flags as risky (leaked credentials, impossible travel...)

Requires Entra ID P2. Use --state atRisk for users that still need action. After investigating, either `risky-users dismiss` (false positive) or `risky-users confirm-compromised`, and reset the password / revoke sessions with the entra users commands. Next: `tenantctl entra risk-detections --user <user>` for the why.

```
tenantctl entra risky-users [options]
```

| Argument  | Type    | Description                                                                                |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--level` | string  | Only this risk level. (one of `low`, `medium`, `high`)                                     |
| `--state` | string  | Only this risk state. (one of `atRisk`, `confirmedCompromised`, `remediated`, `dismissed`) |
| `--top`   | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                  |
| `--all`   | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                               |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra risky-users --state atRisk
tenantctl entra risky-users --level high
```

Permissions: delegated `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All`; application `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All`; role Security Reader

### `tenantctl entra risky-users dismiss`

Dismiss a user's risk after confirming it was a false positive **[write]**

Sets the user risk to none (riskState dismissed) so risk-based Conditional Access stops challenging them. Only do this after reviewing `tenantctl entra risk-detections --user <user>`. Requires Entra ID P2.

```
tenantctl entra risky-users dismiss <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                      |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra risky-users dismiss jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `IdentityRiskyUser.ReadWrite.All`; application `IdentityRiskyUser.ReadWrite.All`; role Security Operator

### `tenantctl entra risky-users confirm-compromised`

Mark a user as confirmed compromised (raises user risk to high) **[destructive]**

Use when an investigation shows the account is in an attacker's hands. Sets user risk to high, so user-risk Conditional Access policies block or force a secure password change. Also reset the password and revoke sessions. Requires Entra ID P2.

```
tenantctl entra risky-users confirm-compromised <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                      |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra risky-users confirm-compromised jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `IdentityRiskyUser.ReadWrite.All`; application `IdentityRiskyUser.ReadWrite.All`; role Security Operator

### `tenantctl entra risk-detections`

Identity Protection risk detections: what made a user or sign-in risky

Each item is one detection (riskEventType such as unfamiliarFeatures, anonymizedIPAddress, leakedCredentials, impossibleTravel) with IP and location. Full detail requires Entra ID P2; P1 tenants see limited detections. Use `correlationId` to find the matching sign-in.

```
tenantctl entra risk-detections [options]
```

| Argument  | Type    | Description                                                  |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--user`  | string  | Only this user (UPN, name or id).                            |
| `--days`  | number  | Look back this many days. (default `7`)                      |
| `--level` | string  | Only this risk level. (one of `low`, `medium`, `high`)       |
| `--top`   | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`   | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra risk-detections --user jane@contoso.com --days 30
tenantctl entra risk-detections --level high
```

Permissions: delegated `IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All`; application `IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All`; role Security Reader

### `tenantctl entra devices list`

List Entra ID device objects; find stale or disabled devices

Entra device objects (identity), not Intune management records. `join` is Entra joined, Hybrid joined or Entra registered (BYOD). `daysSinceSignIn` is approximate (updated about every 14 days). Use --stale-days 90 to find cleanup candidates. For compliance, apps and remote actions use `tenantctl intune devices`.

```
tenantctl entra devices list [options]
```

| Argument       | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--search`     | string  | Words in the device name.                                    |
| `--os`         | string  | Operating system prefix, e.g. Windows, iOS, MacMDM, Android. |
| `--stale-days` | number  | Only devices with no sign-in for at least N days.            |
| `--disabled`   | boolean | Only disabled devices.                                       |
| `--top`        | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`        | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra devices list --stale-days 90 --all
tenantctl entra devices list --os Windows --disabled
```

Permissions: delegated `Device.Read.All`; application `Device.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra devices get`

Show an Entra device with its registered owners and users

Use to see who a device belongs to in Entra and whether it is enabled, compliant and recently active. Accepts name, deviceId (as shown by Intune / dsregcmd) or object id.

```
tenantctl entra devices get <device>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name, deviceId or object id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra devices get DESKTOP-123
```

Permissions: delegated `Device.Read.All`; application `Device.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra devices disable`

Disable an Entra device so it can no longer authenticate (lost or stolen device) **[destructive]**

Blocks the device from Entra sign-in, device-based Conditional Access and SSO; users on it lose access to cloud resources. Does not wipe or retire it in Intune (use `tenantctl intune devices wipe|retire`). Reverse with `tenantctl entra devices enable`. With application permissions only Windows devices can be changed.

```
tenantctl entra devices disable <device>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name, deviceId or object id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra devices disable DESKTOP-123
```

Permissions: delegated `Directory.AccessAsUser.All`; application `Device.ReadWrite.All`; role Cloud Device Administrator

### `tenantctl entra devices enable`

Re-enable a disabled Entra device **[write]**

Restores Entra sign-in for a device disabled with `devices disable`.

```
tenantctl entra devices enable <device>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name, deviceId or object id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra devices enable DESKTOP-123
```

Permissions: delegated `Directory.AccessAsUser.All`; application `Device.ReadWrite.All`; role Cloud Device Administrator

### `tenantctl entra apps consents`

Every delegated grant and application permission an app holds, with ids for revoking

Use for consent reviews and illicit-consent-grant investigations. `delegated` lists OAuth2 permission grants: consent "admin" covers all users, "user" is one user's own consent (principal shown). `application` lists app-only permissions (no user needed; the riskiest kind, e.g. Mail.ReadWrite). Ids (`grantId`, `assignmentId`) feed `apps revoke-consent`. A section shows `{ error }` when a permission is missing.

```
tenantctl entra apps consents <app>
```

| Argument          | Type   | Description                              |
| ----------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `<app>` / `--app` | string | App name, appId or object id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra apps consents "Contoso Mail Sync"
tenantctl entra apps consents 1b2c3d4e-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`; application `Application.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra apps revoke-consent`

Revoke delegated grants and/or application permissions from an app (illicit consent response) **[destructive]**

Illicit-consent-grant playbook: 1) `apps consents <app>` to see what it holds; 2) this command to revoke (--all-delegated --all-application, or pick ids with --grant / --app-role-assignment); 3) `apps disable <app>` so it cannot get new tokens; 4) review what it did: `tenantctl entra signins --app <appId> --days 30` and `tenantctl entra audit --category ApplicationManagement`. Access tokens already issued stay valid until they expire (about an hour); revoke sessions of affected users if needed. Users can consent again unless the app is disabled or user consent is restricted. Preview lists every grant and permission that will be removed.

```
tenantctl entra apps revoke-consent <app> [options]
```

| Argument                | Type     | Description                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<app>` / `--app`       | string   | App name, appId or object id. (required)                                     |
| `--grant`               | string[] | Delegated grant id(s) (grantId from `apps consents`).                        |
| `--all-delegated`       | boolean  | Revoke every delegated grant of the app.                                     |
| `--app-role-assignment` | string[] | Application permission assignment id(s) (assignmentId from `apps consents`). |
| `--all-application`     | boolean  | Revoke every application permission of the app.                              |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra apps revoke-consent "Contoso Mail Sync" --all-delegated --all-application
tenantctl entra apps revoke-consent "Contoso Mail Sync" --grant <grantId>
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`, `DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All`, `AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All`; application `Application.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`, `DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All`, `AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All`; role Cloud Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator

### `tenantctl entra apps disable`

Stop an enterprise app from signing anyone in or getting tokens **[destructive]**

Sets the service principal accountEnabled false: no user can sign in to it and it gets no new tokens, app-only included. Consents and assignments are kept, so `apps enable` undoes it. Use after `apps revoke-consent` for a malicious app, or to pause a misbehaving integration. Tokens already issued stay valid until they expire. Needs Application.ReadWrite.All (Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy only covers apps the caller owns, so it can't disable third-party apps).

```
tenantctl entra apps disable <app>
```

| Argument          | Type   | Description                              |
| ----------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `<app>` / `--app` | string | App name, appId or object id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra apps disable "Contoso Mail Sync"
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.ReadWrite.All`; application `Application.ReadWrite.All`; role Cloud Application Administrator or Application Administrator

### `tenantctl entra apps enable`

Re-enable a disabled enterprise app **[write]**

Sets the service principal accountEnabled true; users and the app can get tokens again.

```
tenantctl entra apps enable <app>
```

| Argument          | Type   | Description                              |
| ----------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `<app>` / `--app` | string | App name, appId or object id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra apps enable "Contoso Mail Sync"
```

Permissions: delegated `Application.ReadWrite.All`; application `Application.ReadWrite.All`; role Cloud Application Administrator or Application Administrator

### `tenantctl entra access-reviews list`

Access review series: what they cover, who reviews, how often, current instance

Use for "are we reviewing guest access / admin roles?". Access reviews need Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance licenses; without them the list is empty or Graph answers 403. `scope` summarizes whose access is reviewed (ids are groups, apps or roles; resolve with `entra groups get` / `entra apps get`). `currentInstance` is the running or most recent instance (`daysLeft` while in progress); `nextInstance` appears when Graph has already scheduled one. Next: `access-reviews decisions <id>`.

```
tenantctl entra access-reviews list [options]
```

| Argument   | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--active` | boolean | Only reviews in progress now.                                |
| `--top`    | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`    | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra access-reviews list
tenantctl entra access-reviews list --active
```

Permissions: delegated `AccessReview.Read.All`; application `AccessReview.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra access-reviews decisions`

Decisions in the current (or latest) instance of an access review

Use for "who still hasn't been reviewed?" or "who was denied?". Access reviews need Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance licenses; without them the list is empty or Graph answers 403. Picks the in-progress instance, else the most recent one (--instance to choose). `decision` is Approve, Deny, DontKnow or NotReviewed; `recommendation` is Graph's suggestion from sign-in activity. --pending shows only NotReviewed. Group-wide reviews of every Microsoft 365 group have one instance per group; pass --instance for others.

```
tenantctl entra access-reviews decisions <review-id> [options]
```

| Argument                      | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<review-id>` / `--review-id` | string  | Review id or name. (required)                                |
| `--pending`                   | boolean | Only decisions not made yet (NotReviewed).                   |
| `--instance`                  | string  | Instance id (default: current or latest).                    |
| `--top`                       | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`                       | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra access-reviews decisions "Quarterly guest review" --pending
tenantctl entra access-reviews decisions <reviewId> --all
```

Permissions: delegated `AccessReview.Read.All`; application `AccessReview.Read.All`

### `tenantctl entra partners`

GDAP relationships this partner tenant holds with customers: roles, expiry, auto-extend

For MSPs (run in the partner tenant): which customer relationships exist, which Entra roles each grants, and when they expire. `daysLeft` counts to endDateTime; `expiringSoon` is true for live relationships ending within 30 days without auto-extend (renew in Partner Center). This Graph API covers the partner side only: in a customer tenant it returns nothing or 403, and Graph has no API listing which partners hold admin access to us (see Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Partner relationships). Role names need RoleManagement.Read.Directory; without it role ids are shown.

```
tenantctl entra partners [options]
```

| Argument   | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--active` | boolean | Only active relationships.                                   |
| `--top`    | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`    | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra partners
tenantctl entra partners --active --all
```

Permissions: delegated `DelegatedAdminRelationship.Read.All`, `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`; application `DelegatedAdminRelationship.Read.All`, `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`

### `tenantctl entra subscriptions`

Commercial subscriptions: seats, trial, status and days until the next lifecycle step

Use for renewals and "why are licenses about to stop working?". `status` Enabled -> Warning (expired, grace) -> Suspended -> Deleted; `nextLifecycleDateTime` is when it moves to the next state if not renewed, `daysToNextLifecycle` counts to it and `renewalSoon` is true under 30 days. Auto-renewing subscriptions also show a date (the renewal). Seat usage per SKU: `tenantctl entra licenses`.

```
tenantctl entra subscriptions [options]
```

| Argument         | Type    | Description                                           |
| ---------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--renewal-soon` | boolean | Only subscriptions within 30 days of their next step. |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl entra subscriptions
tenantctl entra subscriptions --renewal-soon
```

Permissions: delegated `Organization.Read.All`; application `Organization.Read.All`

## intune

Managed devices, compliance, configuration, apps, Autopilot, remote actions

### `tenantctl intune devices list`

List Intune managed devices with filters for user, OS, compliance, staleness and ownership

Start here for "which devices does Jane have", "show non-compliant Windows laptops" or "find devices that stopped checking in". daysSinceLastSync > 30 usually means the device is lost, retired or reimaged. --compliance and --stale-days are filtered by Graph; --user/--os/--ownership use filters Intune accepts but does not document, and fall back to client-side filtering (slower) if Graph rejects them. --search is always applied client-side, so pair it with another filter in a large tenant. Next: `devices get` for detail, `devices compliance` for why a device is non-compliant.

```
tenantctl intune devices list [options]
```

| Argument       | Type    | Description                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--user`       | string  | Primary user (UPN, mail, name or id).                                                                   |
| `--os`         | string  | Platform. (one of `windows`, `ios`, `android`, `macos`, `linux`)                                        |
| `--compliance` | string  | Compliance state. (one of `compliant`, `noncompliant`, `ingraceperiod`, `unknown`, `error`, `conflict`) |
| `--stale-days` | number  | Only devices that have not synced for at least N days.                                                  |
| `--search`     | string  | Device name prefix or exact serial number.                                                              |
| `--ownership`  | string  | Corporate or personal. (one of `company`, `personal`)                                                   |
| `--top`        | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                               |
| `--all`        | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                            |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune devices list --user jane@contoso.com
tenantctl intune devices list --os windows --compliance noncompliant
tenantctl intune devices list --stale-days 30 --all
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl intune devices get`

Show one device in detail: hardware, storage, encryption, enrollment, primary user, Defender health

Use when troubleshooting a specific device. storage.percentFree under 10 often explains failed updates and app installs. defender (Windows only) shows antivirus health as Intune last saw it; signatureUpdateOverdue or realTimeProtectionEnabled=false are red flags. autopilotEnrolled/joinType come from the beta API. Sections that fail (e.g. missing permission) appear as { error } without hiding the rest.

```
tenantctl intune devices get <device>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name, serial number, Intune device id or Entra device id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune devices get DESKTOP-4F2K9
tenantctl intune devices get 5CG1234XYZ
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl intune devices compliance`

Explain why a device is (non-)compliant: per-policy state and the failing settings

Use for "why is my laptop non-compliant" or "why is Conditional Access blocking this device". `summary` is a sentence you can relay to the user; `policies[].failingSettings` lists each failing setting with its current value or error. Failures of the built-in "Default Device Compliance Policy" (no check-in, user deleted, no policy assigned) carry a `reason`. If nothing fails but the device is not compliant, run `devices sync` and re-check after a few minutes.

```
tenantctl intune devices compliance <device>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name, serial number, Intune device id or Entra device id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune devices compliance DESKTOP-4F2K9
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl intune devices config-states`

Show configuration profile states on a device, with errors and conflicts first

Use when a setting (Wi-Fi, VPN, BitLocker, restrictions) did not apply to a device. `problems` lists profiles in error or conflict with their failing settings; a conflict means two profiles set the same setting to different values. Covers classic configuration profiles; settings catalog policies may not appear here.

```
tenantctl intune devices config-states <device>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name, serial number, Intune device id or Entra device id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune devices config-states DESKTOP-4F2K9
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator or Global Reader

List software Intune detected on a device (inventory, not install status)

Answers "what version of Chrome is on this laptop" or "is Zoom installed". This is the discovered-apps inventory the device last reported, not whether an Intune-assigned app installed successfully (use `apps status <app>` for that). Personal iOS/Android devices only report managed apps. (beta API)

| `--search`              | string  | Substring of the app name or publisher.                                     |
| `--top`                 | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                   |
| `--all`                 | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                |

```sh
tenantctl intune devices apps DESKTOP-4F2K9 --search chrome
```

### `tenantctl intune devices bitlocker-key`

List BitLocker recovery keys escrowed in Entra for a device; --reveal shows the keys

Use when a user is stuck at the BitLocker recovery screen: match the key id shown on screen (first 8 characters) to `items[].id`, then rerun with --reveal. Without --reveal only key ids, creation time and volume type are returned. Each revealed key is logged as "Read BitLocker key" in the Entra audit log. Needs BitlockerKey.Read.All (BitlockerKey.ReadBasic.All suffices without --reveal) and, delegated, a role such as Cloud Device Administrator, Helpdesk Administrator or Intune Administrator. No keys usually means the device never backed up to Entra; rotate with `devices rotate-bitlocker`.

```

```

| Argument                | Type    | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string  | Device name, serial number, Intune device id or Entra device id. (required) |
| `--reveal`              | boolean | Include the secret itself. Every reveal is recorded in the Entra audit log. |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune devices bitlocker-key DESKTOP-4F2K9
tenantctl intune devices bitlocker-key DESKTOP-4F2K9 --reveal
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `BitlockerKey.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `BitlockerKey.Read.All`; role Cloud Device Administrator or Helpdesk Administrator or Intune Administrator or Security Reader

### `tenantctl intune devices laps`

Show the Windows LAPS local admin account backed up to Entra; --reveal shows the password

Use when someone needs local admin on a Windows device. Without --reveal returns the last backup and next rotation time only; --reveal adds the account name and decoded password (newest first). Reveals are logged in the Entra audit log. Not found means Windows LAPS is not configured to back up to Entra for this device. Rotate with `devices rotate-laps`.

### `tenantctl intune apps assign`

Assign a app to a group, all users or all devices (keeps existing assignments) **[destructive]**

Adds one target to the app's assignments; existing assignments are read first and kept, because Intune's assign action replaces the whole list. intent required installs the app on targeted devices/users, available offers it in Company Portal (users only: refused with --all-devices, and Intune ignores available for device groups), uninstall removes it. A group already assigned with another intent is switched to the new one. Assignment settings (delivery optimisation, notifications) take Intune defaults; adjust them in the admin center. The preview shows the target group with its member count, the current assignments and the resulting list.

```
tenantctl intune apps assign <item> --intent <string> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<item>` / `--item` | string  | App name or id. (required)                                                                                                       |
| `--intent`          | string  | required (install), available (Company Portal, users only) or uninstall. (required; one of `required`, `available`, `uninstall`) |
| `--group`           | string  | Target group: name, mail or id.                                                                                                  |
| `--all-users`       | boolean | Target all licensed users.                                                                                                       |
| `--all-devices`     | boolean | Target all Intune-managed devices.                                                                                               |
| `--exclude`         | string  | Exclude this group (name, mail or id).                                                                                           |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune apps assign "Zoom Workplace" --intent required --group "Sales Laptops"
tenantctl intune apps assign "Company Portal" --intent available --all-users --exclude "Kiosk Users"
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator

### `tenantctl intune apps unassign`

Remove one target from a app's assignments (keeps the others) **[destructive]**

Removes only the assignment for the given group (or all users / all devices / the exclusion); the other assignments are re-sent unchanged. Removing a required app assignment does not uninstall the app; assign it with --intent uninstall for that.

```
tenantctl intune apps unassign <item> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<item>` / `--item` | string  | App name or id. (required)                                                                 |
| `--group`           | string  | Target group: name, mail or id.                                                            |
| `--all-users`       | boolean | Target all licensed users.                                                                 |
| `--all-devices`     | boolean | Target all Intune-managed devices.                                                         |
| `--exclude`         | string  | Remove the exclusion of this group instead.                                                |
| `--intent`          | string  | Only remove the assignment with this intent. (one of `required`, `available`, `uninstall`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune apps unassign "Zoom Workplace" --group "Sales Laptops"
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator

### `tenantctl intune compliance assign`

Assign a compliance policy to a group, all users or all devices (keeps existing assignments) **[destructive]**

Adds one target to the compliance policy's assignments; existing assignments are read first and kept, because Intune's assign action replaces the whole list. Newly targeted devices are evaluated at their next check-in; non-compliant ones can lose access through Conditional Access after the grace period. The preview shows the target group with its member count, the current assignments and the resulting list.

```
tenantctl intune compliance assign <item> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                              |
| ------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `<item>` / `--item` | string  | Compliance policy name or id. (required) |
| `--group`           | string  | Target group: name, mail or id.          |
| `--all-users`       | boolean | Target all licensed users.               |
| `--all-devices`     | boolean | Target all Intune-managed devices.       |
| `--exclude`         | string  | Exclude this group (name, mail or id).   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune compliance assign "Windows baseline" --group "All Windows" --exclude "Kiosks"
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator

### `tenantctl intune assignments`

Which apps, compliance policies and configuration profiles target a group

Answers "what will a device or user in group X get?". Scans every app, compliance policy, classic configuration profile and settings catalog policy (beta) and reads their assignments through $batch. included = targets this group or a group it is nested in (via names the parent); excluded = this group is excluded; allUsers/allDevices = applies to everyone regardless of group. --max-items caps how many apps/policies are scanned (truncated=true when hit). Sections Graph refused are listed in unavailable.

```
tenantctl intune assignments <group> [options]
```

| Argument              | Type   | Description                                      |
| --------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `<group>` / `--group` | string | Group name, mail or id. (required)               |
| `--max-items`         | number | Maximum apps + policies to scan. (default `500`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl intune assignments "Sales Laptops"
tenantctl intune assignments "All Staff" --max-items 2000
```

Permissions: delegated `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; role Intune Administrator or Global Reader

## defender

Incidents, alerts, hunting, Secure Score, device response (isolate, scan, investigate)

### `tenantctl defender incidents list`

List Defender XDR incidents (correlated alerts), newest first

Start here for "is anything going on?" or "what is open?". Each row is an incident: a group of related alerts across Defender products. alertCount shows how many alerts it groups; status active means nobody closed it; redirected means it was merged into another incident. Use --unassigned to find work nobody owns. Next: `tenantctl defender incidents get <id>` for alerts and affected users/devices. Needs Microsoft Defender XDR (any Defender product: Defender for Endpoint P2, Office 365 P2, Identity or Cloud Apps, e.g. via Microsoft 365 E5 / E5 Security).

```
tenantctl defender incidents list [options]
```

| Argument        | Type    | Description                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--status`      | string  | Only this status. (one of `active`, `inProgress`, `resolved`, `redirected`) |
| `--severity`    | string  | Only this severity. (one of `informational`, `low`, `medium`, `high`)       |
| `--days`        | number  | Only items created in the last N days.                                      |
| `--assigned-to` | string  | Only incidents owned by this person (UPN as shown in Defender).             |
| `--unassigned`  | boolean | Only incidents with no owner.                                               |
| `--top`         | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                   |
| `--all`         | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender incidents list --status active --severity high
tenantctl defender incidents list --days 7 --unassigned
```

Permissions: delegated `SecurityIncident.Read.All`; application `SecurityIncident.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender incidents get`

Show an incident with its alerts, affected entities and comments

Use to explain an incident: what fired (alerts with severity, product, category and MITRE techniques), who and what is involved (entities: users, devices, IPs, mailboxes, files, URLs, emails, apps, merged across all alerts) and what analysts said (comments). Next: investigate a user with `tenantctl entra users get`, a device with `tenantctl intune devices get`, or close the incident with `tenantctl defender incidents update <id> --status resolved --classification ...`.

```
tenantctl defender incidents get <id>
```

| Argument        | Type   | Description             |
| --------------- | ------ | ----------------------- |
| `<id>` / `--id` | string | Incident id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender incidents get 3962396
```

Permissions: delegated `SecurityIncident.Read.All`; application `SecurityIncident.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender incidents update`

Assign, triage, resolve or comment on an incident **[write]**

Only the options you pass change. Resolving: --status resolved with --classification (truePositive, falsePositive, informationalExpectedActivity) and a matching --determination. --assign-to takes the owner as free text (normally a UPN); "none" clears it. --comment is added to the incident activity log. Updating an incident also updates its alerts.

```
tenantctl defender incidents update <id> [options]
```

| Argument           | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<id>` / `--id`    | string | Incident id. (required)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--status`         | string | New status. (one of `active`, `inProgress`, `resolved`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--assign-to`      | string | Owner (UPN or free text); "none" unassigns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--classification` | string | Verdict: truePositive (real threat), falsePositive, informationalExpectedActivity (benign), unknown. (one of `unknown`, `falsePositive`, `truePositive`, `informationalExpectedActivity`)                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--determination`  | string | What it was, e.g. phishing, malware, compromisedAccount, notMalicious, securityTesting. (one of `unknown`, `apt`, `malware`, `securityPersonnel`, `securityTesting`, `unwantedSoftware`, `other`, `multiStagedAttack`, `compromisedAccount`, `phishing`, `maliciousUserActivity`, `notMalicious`, `notEnoughDataToValidate`, `confirmedActivity`, `lineOfBusinessApplication`) |
| `--comment`        | string | Add a comment to the activity log.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender incidents update 3962396 --assign-to secops@contoso.com --status inProgress
tenantctl defender incidents update 3962396 --status resolved --classification falsePositive --determination notMalicious --comment "Pen test"
```

Permissions: delegated `SecurityIncident.ReadWrite.All`; application `SecurityIncident.ReadWrite.All`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender alerts list`

List Defender alerts from all Microsoft security products

Alerts are individual detections (an incident groups several). user/device are the first ones named in the evidence. Filter by --source to one product (e.g. microsoftDefenderForOffice365 for email threats, azureAdIdentityProtection for risky sign-ins). --category (e.g. InitialAccess, Execution, CredentialAccess) is matched client-side, so it pages until enough matches are found; combine it with --days. Next: `tenantctl defender alerts get <id>` or `incidents get <incidentId>`. Needs Microsoft Defender XDR (any Defender product: Defender for Endpoint P2, Office 365 P2, Identity or Cloud Apps, e.g. via Microsoft 365 E5 / E5 Security).

```
tenantctl defender alerts list [options]
```

| Argument     | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--severity` | string  | Only this severity. (one of `informational`, `low`, `medium`, `high`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--status`   | string  | Only this status. (one of `new`, `inProgress`, `resolved`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--source`   | string  | Only alerts from this product. (one of `microsoftDefenderForEndpoint`, `microsoftDefenderForIdentity`, `microsoftDefenderForCloudApps`, `microsoftDefenderForOffice365`, `microsoft365Defender`, `azureAdIdentityProtection`, `microsoftAppGovernance`, `dataLossPrevention`, `microsoftDefenderForCloud`, `microsoftSentinel`, `microsoftThreatIntelligence`, `microsoftSecurityForAI`) |
| `--days`     | number  | Only items created in the last N days.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--category` | string  | MITRE ATT&CK tactic, e.g. InitialAccess, Execution.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--top`      | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--all`      | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender alerts list --status new --severity high
tenantctl defender alerts list --source microsoftDefenderForOffice365 --days 7
```

Permissions: delegated `SecurityAlert.Read.All`; application `SecurityAlert.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

entities summarizes the evidence (users, devices, IPs, mailboxes, files, URLs, emails, apps). recommendedActions is the product's remediation advice. Next: `incidents get <incidentId>` for the wider picture, or `alerts update <id>` to triage.

```

(one of `unknown`, `falsePositive`, `truePositive`, `informationalExpectedActivity`)                                                                                                                                                                                      |

(one of `unknown`, `apt`, `malware`, `securityPersonnel`, `securityTesting`, `unwantedSoftware`, `other`, `multiStagedAttack`, `compromisedAccount`, `phishing`, `maliciousUserActivity`, `notMalicious`, `notEnoughDataToValidate`, `confirmedActivity`, `lineOfBusinessApplication`) |
| `--comment`        | string | Add a comment to the activity log.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

### `tenantctl defender alerts for-user`

Alerts that involve a user, across all Defender products

Runs the alerts-for-user hunting query (AlertEvidence joined to AlertInfo) and looks each alert up to add its status and incident. Use when asked "has anything flagged Jane?". Matches evidence by UPN or object id. Hunting data covers at most 30 days. Needs Microsoft Defender XDR (any Defender product: Defender for Endpoint P2, Office 365 P2, Identity or Cloud Apps, e.g. via Microsoft 365 E5 / E5 Security).

```
tenantctl defender alerts for-user <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                       |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | UPN, email, name or id. (required)                |
| `--days`            | number | Look back this many days (max 30). (default `30`) |
| `--top`             | number | Maximum alerts to return. (default `25`)          |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender alerts for-user jane@contoso.com --days 7
```

Permissions: delegated `ThreatHunting.Read.All`, `SecurityAlert.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `ThreatHunting.Read.All`, `SecurityAlert.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender alerts for-device`

Alerts that involve a device, across all Defender products

Runs the alerts-for-device hunting query and adds each alert's status and incident. The device is matched by name (short name or FQDN) or Defender device id, as Defender knows it; no Intune lookup. Hunting data covers at most 30 days. Needs Microsoft Defender XDR (any Defender product: Defender for Endpoint P2, Office 365 P2, Identity or Cloud Apps, e.g. via Microsoft 365 E5 / E5 Security).

```
tenantctl defender alerts for-device <device> [options]
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                       |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `<device>` / `--device` | string | Device name or id. (required)                     |
| `--days`                | number | Look back this many days (max 30). (default `30`) |
| `--top`                 | number | Maximum alerts to return. (default `25`)          |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender alerts for-device DESKTOP-123 --days 14
```

Permissions: delegated `ThreatHunting.Read.All`, `SecurityAlert.Read.All`; application `ThreatHunting.Read.All`, `SecurityAlert.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender hunt`

Run an advanced hunting (KQL) query or a curated template

Pass KQL directly, or --template <name> with --param key=value (see `tenantctl defender hunt templates`). Template values are inserted as escaped KQL string literals. Output: columns (name, type) and rows. Graph returns up to 100,000 rows; this command shows the first --top, so add `| take`, `| summarize` or `| project` to keep results small. Data reaches back 30 days (default timespan). Long-running or expensive queries can be throttled (429) per tenant CPU quota. Read-only even though it is a POST. Needs Microsoft Defender XDR (any Defender product: Defender for Endpoint P2, Office 365 P2, Identity or Cloud Apps, e.g. via Microsoft 365 E5 / E5 Security).

```
tenantctl defender hunt [query] [options]
```

| Argument              | Type     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<query>` / `--query` | string   | KQL query (omit when using --template).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--template`          | string   | Curated query name. (one of `signins-for-user`, `emails-from-sender`, `email-by-subject`, `url-clicks-for-user`, `device-processes`, `device-network`, `device-logons`, `alerts-for-user`, `alerts-for-device`, `file-hash-prevalence`, `inbox-rule-changes`) |
| `--param`             | string[] | Template parameter as name=value; repeat --param for each key=value.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--timespan`          | string   | How far back to look: ISO 8601 duration (P7D, PT12H), an interval (2026-01-01T00:00:00Z/P7D), or shorthand like 7d. Default 30 days.                                                                                                                          |
| `--top`               | number   | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--all`               | boolean  | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender hunt "DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName | take 10"
tenantctl defender hunt --template emails-from-sender --param sender=bad@evil.example --timespan P7D
```

Permissions: delegated `ThreatHunting.Read.All`; application `ThreatHunting.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender hunt templates`

List curated hunting queries and their parameters

Each template answers a common question (sign-ins for a user, emails from a sender, processes on a device...). Run one with `tenantctl defender hunt --template <name> --param key=value`. requires names the product whose data the table needs; an empty result can mean that product is not licensed.

```
tenantctl defender hunt templates
```

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender hunt templates
```

### `tenantctl defender secure-score`

Show Microsoft Secure Score and the improvement actions worth the most points

percent is currentScore / maxScore. comparison holds average scores for all tenants, tenants of similar size (totalSeats) and the same industry. topActions ranks controls by points still available (remainingPoints) with cost, user impact and a portal link (actionUrl). Use for "how secure are we?" and "what should we fix first?". Scores are calculated daily.

```
tenantctl defender secure-score [options]
```

| Argument        | Type   | Description                                          |
| --------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `--top-actions` | number | How many improvement actions to show. (default `10`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender secure-score
tenantctl defender secure-score --top-actions 5
```

Permissions: delegated `SecurityEvents.Read.All`; application `SecurityEvents.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Global Reader or Security Administrator

Submit an email to Microsoft for analysis as phishing, spam, malware or not junk (beta API) **[write]**

Microsoft re-scans it; the result (status, result.category, result.detail) appears on the returned submission after a while. Needs Defender for Office 365 or Exchange Online Protection. (beta API)

| `--category`                    | string | What the message is. (required; one of `phishing`, `spam`, `malware`, `notJunk`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender threat-submit email jane@contoso.com AAMkADU3MWUxOTU0... --category phishing

Permissions: delegated `ThreatSubmission.ReadWrite`, `User.Read.All`; application `ThreatSubmission.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines list`

List Defender for Endpoint machines with health, risk, exposure and last seen

Device inventory as Defender for Endpoint sees it. --search matches the start of the computer name; --risk filters riskScore (High/Medium/Low); --health active|inactive filters healthStatus; --os takes an osPlatform value (Windows11, Windows10, WindowsServer2022, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android...); --stale-days lists machines not seen for N days. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines list [options]
```

| Argument       | Type    | Description                                                   |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--search`     | string  | Computer name prefix.                                         |
| `--risk`       | string  | Only this risk score. (one of `high`, `medium`, `low`)        |
| `--health`     | string  | Only this sensor health status. (one of `active`, `inactive`) |
| `--os`         | string  | osPlatform, e.g. Windows11, WindowsServer2022, Linux, macOS.  |
| `--stale-days` | number  | Only machines not seen in the last N days.                    |
| `--top`        | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                     |
| `--all`        | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines list --risk high
tenantctl defender machines list --health inactive --stale-days 30 --all
tenantctl defender machines list --search laptop-7
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines get`

One Defender machine: health, risk, open alerts and recent response actions

Accepts the computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id. openAlerts counts alerts not yet resolved (needs Alert.ReadWrite.All per the MDE docs); recentActions lists the last 10 response actions (needs Machine.ReadWrite.All). A section the token lacks degrades to { error }. Next: `defender alerts for-device <name>` or a response action. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```

```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines get LAPTOP-7
tenantctl defender machines get 7f3a1d8e-0000-4c1b-9a1e-1234567890ab
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.ReadWrite.All`, `Alert.ReadWrite.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines isolate`

Isolate a machine from the network (Defender keeps its connection to the service) **[destructive]**

Use when a device is compromised or actively attacked. Full isolation cuts all network traffic except to Defender for Endpoint; --selective (Windows only) still lets Outlook, Teams and Skype communicate. Machines behind a full-tunnel VPN can lose contact with Defender once isolated. Undo with `machines release`. Supported: Windows 10 1703+/11 (selective 1709+), Windows Server, Linux. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines isolate <machine> --comment <string> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string  | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |
| `--selective`             | boolean | Selective isolation (Outlook/Teams keep working).                               |
| `--comment`               | string  | Why (recorded in the Defender action center). (required)                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines isolate LAPTOP-7 --comment "Ransomware alert 1234"
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.Isolate`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines release`

Release a machine from network isolation **[write]**

Undoes `machines isolate`. The machine reconnects once it receives the request. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines release <machine> --comment <string>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |
| `--comment`               | string | Why (recorded in the Defender action center). (required)                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines release LAPTOP-7 --comment "Remediated, cleared by SOC"
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.Isolate`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines scan`

Run a Microsoft Defender Antivirus quick or full scan on a machine **[write]**

Quick scan by default; --full-scan scans every file and can take hours. Works with Defender Antivirus in passive mode too. Supported: Windows 10 1709+/11, Windows Server, Linux, macOS. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines scan <machine> --comment <string> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string  | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |
| `--full-scan`             | boolean | Full scan instead of a quick scan.                                              |
| `--comment`               | string  | Why (recorded in the Defender action center). (required)                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines scan LAPTOP-7 --full-scan --comment "Alert 1234 follow-up"
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.Scan`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines collect-package`

Collect an investigation package (logs, processes, network state) from a machine **[write]**

Use for forensics. When the action status is Succeeded, get a download link with `machines package-url <actionId>`. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines collect-package <machine> --comment <string>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |
| `--comment`               | string | Why (recorded in the Defender action center). (required)                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines collect-package LAPTOP-7 --comment "Incident 42 forensics"
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.CollectForensics`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines restrict`

Restrict app execution on a machine to Microsoft-signed binaries **[destructive]**

Containment for an active threat: only files signed by Microsoft can run until `machines unrestrict`. Needs Microsoft Defender Antivirus. Supported: Windows 10 1709+/11. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines restrict <machine> --comment <string>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |
| `--comment`               | string | Why (recorded in the Defender action center). (required)                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines restrict LAPTOP-7 --comment "Unknown binary spreading"
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.RestrictExecution`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines unrestrict`

Remove the app execution restriction from a machine **[write]**

Undoes `machines restrict`. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines unrestrict <machine> --comment <string>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |
| `--comment`               | string | Why (recorded in the Defender action center). (required)                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines unrestrict LAPTOP-7 --comment "Threat removed"
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.RestrictExecution`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines stop-quarantine-file`

Stop a running file on a machine and quarantine it (by SHA-1) **[destructive]**

Kills processes of the file and moves it to quarantine. Refused by Defender for files signed by Microsoft or trusted publishers. Needs Defender Antivirus (passive mode is enough). Supported: Windows 10 1703+/11. Find the SHA-1 in alert evidence or `tenantctl defender hunt`. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines stop-quarantine-file <machine> --sha1 <string> --comment <string>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<machine>` / `--machine` | string | Computer name, Defender machine id or Entra device id (aadDeviceId). (required) |
| `--sha1`                  | string | SHA-1 of the file (40 hex characters). (required)                               |
| `--comment`               | string | Why (recorded in the Defender action center). (required)                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines stop-quarantine-file LAPTOP-7 --sha1 a0c659857ccbe457fdaf5fe21d54efdcbf6f6508 --comment "Malware from alert 99"
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.Read.All`, `Machine.StopAndQuarantine`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines package-url`

Download link for a collected investigation package

Pass the machine action id returned by `machines collect-package`. The link is short-lived: download it right away. Answers NOT_FOUND while the collection is still running; check with `machines actions`. Defender limits this call to 2 per minute. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines package-url <action-id>
```

| Argument                      | Type   | Description                   |
| ----------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------- |
| `<action-id>` / `--action-id` | string | Machine action id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines package-url 69dc3630-1ccc-4342-acf3-35286eec741d
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.ReadWrite.All`, `Machine.CollectForensics`; role Security Operator or Security Administrator

### `tenantctl defender machines actions`

Response actions (isolate, scan, collect...) and their status, newest first

Use to follow up on an action id returned by a `machines` response command, or to see what was done to a machine. status is Pending, InProgress, Succeeded, Failed, TimeOut or Cancelled. Needs Machine.ReadWrite.All per the MDE docs. Needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Defender for Business. Delegated use requires your own app registration with WindowsDefenderATP delegated permissions.

```
tenantctl defender machines actions [options]
```

| Argument    | Type    | Description                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--machine` | string  | Only actions on this machine (name or id).                                                                   |
| `--status`  | string  | Only actions in this status. (one of `Pending`, `InProgress`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `TimeOut`, `Cancelled`) |
| `--top`     | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                    |
| `--all`     | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                 |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl defender machines actions --machine LAPTOP-7
tenantctl defender machines actions --status Pending
```

Permissions: Defender for Endpoint `Machine.ReadWrite.All`; role Security Reader or Security Operator or Security Administrator

## exchange

Mailboxes, rules, forwarding, permissions, shared mailboxes, DLs, quarantine, holds, trace, rooms

### `tenantctl exchange mailbox`

Mailbox overview: type, time zone, auto-reply, working hours, folder counts

First stop for any mailbox question. userPurpose tells user/shared/room/equipment mailboxes apart. autoReplyOn is the effective out-of-office state right now (null when scheduled in a non-UTC zone). folders gives total/unread item counts for Inbox, Sent, Deleted and Junk (folder sizes are not exposed by Graph v1.0; use `tenantctl exchange usage --user` for storage). Each section degrades to { error } on its own. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange mailbox <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange mailbox jane@contoso.com
tenantctl exchange mailbox "Conference Room A"
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `User.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange auto-reply get`

Show a mailbox's automatic replies (out of office)

status is disabled, alwaysEnabled or scheduled; autoReplyOn is whether replies go out right now. Messages are shown as plain text (use --full for the HTML). Change it with `tenantctl exchange auto-reply set`. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange auto-reply get <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                   |
