| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange auto-reply get jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange auto-reply set`

Turn automatic replies (out of office) on, off or scheduled **[write]**

Pass exactly one of --on, --off, --scheduled (or none to only change messages/audience). --scheduled needs --start and --end: times with Z or an offset are converted to UTC; times without one are read in --time-zone or, by default, the mailbox time zone. Messages accept plain text or HTML. --external-audience: none (no external replies), contactsOnly, all. Common for leavers: set it on with a redirect message, then `tenantctl exchange auto-reply get` to confirm. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange auto-reply set <user> [options]
```

| Argument              | Type    | Description                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user`   | string  | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required)                |
| `--on`                | boolean | Always send automatic replies.                                                               |
| `--off`               | boolean | Stop automatic replies.                                                                      |
| `--scheduled`         | boolean | Send automatic replies between --start and --end.                                            |
| `--start`             | string  | Schedule start, ISO (2026-12-20T17:00 or with Z/offset).                                     |
| `--end`               | string  | Schedule end, ISO.                                                                           |
| `--time-zone`         | string  | Time zone for --start/--end without an offset (default: mailbox time zone).                  |
| `--internal-message`  | string  | Reply sent to people inside the organization.                                                |
| `--external-message`  | string  | Reply sent to external senders.                                                              |
| `--external-audience` | string  | Who outside the organization gets the external reply. (one of `none`, `contactsOnly`, `all`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange auto-reply set jane@contoso.com --on --internal-message "I am out until Monday."
tenantctl exchange auto-reply set jane@contoso.com --scheduled --start 2026-12-20T17:00 --end 2027-01-05T08:00 --external-audience all --external-message "Out of office."
tenantctl exchange auto-reply set jane@contoso.com --off
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite`, `User.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange messages search`

Find messages in a mailbox by sender, subject, date, folder (metadata only)

Use for "did Jane receive the invoice from X?" or to locate a phishing message before purging it. Returns metadata only, never bodies. --from with a full address and no --subject uses an exact $filter sorted newest first; --subject or a sender name uses Outlook keyword search (word matches, sorted by sent date, at most 1000 results). Pass the `id` (or internetMessageId) to `tenantctl exchange messages delete`. For "did it arrive at all", use `tenantctl exchange trace` instead. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange messages search <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string  | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--from`            | string  | Sender address or name.                                                       |
| `--subject`         | string  | Words that must appear in the subject.                                        |
| `--since`           | number  | Only messages received in the last N days. (default `30`)                     |
| `--folder`          | string  | inbox, sent, deleted, junk, archive, drafts, or a top-level folder name.      |
| `--has-attachments` | boolean | Only messages with (non-inline) attachments.                                  |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                     |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange messages search jane@contoso.com --from billing@vendor.com --since 7
tenantctl exchange messages search jane@contoso.com --subject "invoice overdue" --folder junk
```

Permissions: delegated `Mail.ReadBasic`, `User.Read.All`; application `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange messages delete`

Delete a message from a mailbox (incident response purge) **[destructive]**

Removes a phishing or misdirected message. Default moves it to Deleted Items (recoverable by the user); --hard permanently deletes it (moves it to Recoverable Items > Purges; the user cannot restore it). Accepts a Graph message id from `messages search` or an Internet Message-ID (<...@...>) from `trace`. One mailbox per call: repeat per recipient. For tenant-wide purges use Microsoft Purview / Defender Threat Explorer. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange messages delete <user> <message> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user`       | string  | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `<message>` / `--message` | string  | Message id or Internet Message-ID. (required)                                 |
| `--hard`                  | boolean | Permanently delete instead of moving to Deleted Items.                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange messages delete jane@contoso.com AAMkAGI2...
tenantctl exchange messages delete jane@contoso.com "<abc123@phish.example>" --hard
```

Permissions: delegated `Mail.ReadWrite`, `User.Read.All`; application `Mail.ReadWrite`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange calendar permissions`

Who can see or edit a user's primary calendar

role: freeBusyRead (free/busy only), limitedRead (+ titles/locations), read (all details), write (edit), delegateWithoutPrivateEventAccess / delegateWithPrivateEventAccess (delegates who also get meeting messages), custom. "My Organization" has no address and is the default for everyone internal. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange calendar permissions <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange calendar permissions jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Calendars.ReadBasic`, `User.Read.All`; application `Calendars.ReadBasic`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange calendar events`

List a user's meetings for the next N days, in the mailbox time zone

Expands recurring meetings into occurrences. Times are in the mailbox time zone (shown in timeZone) when it can be read, else UTC. Useful for "is Jane free Thursday" or checking a room mailbox's bookings. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange calendar events <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string  | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `--days`            | number  | Days ahead to include, from now. (default `7`)                                |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                     |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange calendar events jane@contoso.com --days 3
```

Permissions: delegated `Calendars.ReadBasic`, `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`; application `Calendars.ReadBasic`, `MailboxSettings.Read`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange rules list`

List a mailbox's inbox rules with forwarding and BEC red flags

Use when mail goes missing, a user says replies vanish, or you suspect a compromised account. Each rule has readable conditions/actions plus derived flags: forwards, forwardsExternally (target domain not a verified tenant domain), deletes, movesToFolder, marksRead, and suspicious with a reason (external forwarding, or delete/move-to-RSS/Archive combined with mark-as-read or payment keywords: classic business email compromise). Suspicious rule on an account: check `tenantctl entra users signins <user>`, then `tenantctl exchange rules delete`. Only Outlook inbox rules are visible; mailbox-level forwarding is not (see `tenantctl exchange forwarding`). Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange rules list <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange rules list jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `Domain.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange rules delete`

Delete an inbox rule (e.g. a malicious forwarding rule) **[destructive]**

Incident response: removes the rule permanently. Previews the rule first. Consider `rules disable` if you want to keep it for investigation. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange rules delete <user> <rule>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `<rule>` / `--rule` | string | Rule id or name (from `exchange rules list`). (required)                      |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange rules delete jane@contoso.com "."
tenantctl exchange rules delete jane@contoso.com AQAAAJ5...
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `User.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange rules disable`

Turn off an inbox rule without deleting it **[write]**

Stops a rule from running while keeping it for investigation; re-enable it in Outlook or with `tenantctl graph patch`. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange rules disable <user> <rule>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |
| `<rule>` / `--rule` | string | Rule id or name (from `exchange rules list`). (required)                      |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange rules disable jane@contoso.com "Move invoices"
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `User.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange rules audit`

Scan many mailboxes for forwarding or suspicious inbox rules

Tenant-wide BEC sweep. Scans the given users, a group, or (default) licensed member users up to --max-users, batched 20 mailboxes per Graph call, and returns only mailboxes whose rules forward mail or look suspicious. `errors` lists mailboxes that could not be read (no Exchange mailbox, no access). `usersTruncated: true` means more users exist than --max-users. Needs app-only auth to read other mailboxes. Follow up with `tenantctl exchange rules list <user>`.

```
tenantctl exchange rules audit [options]
```

| Argument      | Type     | Description                                           |
| ------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--users`     | string[] | Comma-separated users to scan.                        |
| `--group`     | string   | Scan members of this group (nested members included). |
| `--max-users` | number   | Maximum mailboxes to scan. (default `200`)            |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange rules audit
tenantctl exchange rules audit --group "Finance Team"
tenantctl exchange rules audit --users jane@contoso.com,bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `Domain.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange forwarding`

Show every mail forwarding path of a mailbox: inbox rules and mailbox-level forwarding

Answers "is this mailbox forwarding mail anywhere?". Lists inbox rules that forward or redirect (Graph), and mailbox-level forwarding (ForwardingSmtpAddress / ForwardingAddress, set by admins or in OWA settings) read through the Exchange Online PowerShell bridge. forwardsExternally covers both (null when tenant domains are unreadable). When the bridge is unavailable (no pwsh, not signed in to Exchange, no Exchange role) `mailboxForwarding` is `{ error, hint }` and the inbox-rule result still stands. Change mailbox forwarding with `tenantctl exchange forwarding set|clear`. Reading or changing another person's mailbox needs app-only auth (application permissions); a delegated sign-in only reaches your own mailbox and mailboxes shared with you.

```
tenantctl exchange forwarding <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Mailbox owner: UPN, email/alias, display name, object id, or "me". (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange forwarding jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic`, `Domain.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `MailboxSettings.Read`, `Mail.ReadBasic.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`)

### `tenantctl exchange forwarding set`

Forward all mail of a mailbox to an address (mailbox-level forwarding) **[destructive]**

Sets ForwardingSmtpAddress so every message to the mailbox is forwarded, e.g. a leaver's mail to their manager. Without --keep-copy the mailbox keeps no copy. Destructive because mail leaves the mailbox; the preview shows current forwarding and whether the target is external (external forwarding may also be blocked by the outbound spam policy). Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange forwarding set <mailbox> --to <string> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                               |
| ------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string  | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required)    |
| `--to`                    | string  | SMTP address to forward to. (required)                    |
| `--keep-copy`             | boolean | Also deliver to the mailbox (DeliverToMailboxAndForward). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange forwarding set jane@contoso.com --to bob@contoso.com --keep-copy
```

Permissions: delegated `Domain.Read.All`; application `Domain.Read.All`; Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange forwarding clear`

Remove mailbox-level forwarding **[destructive]**

Clears ForwardingSmtpAddress and ForwardingAddress and turns DeliverToMailboxAndForward off. Inbox-rule forwarding is separate: see `tenantctl exchange forwarding <mailbox>` and `exchange rules delete`. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange forwarding clear <mailbox>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange forwarding clear jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange permissions list`

Who has FullAccess, Send As or Send on Behalf on a mailbox

One flat list `{ user, access }` from Get-MailboxPermission (FullAccess), Get-RecipientPermission (SendAs) and GrantSendOnBehalfTo. The mailbox owner (NT AUTHORITY\SELF) and inherited/system entries are left out unless --include-inherited. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange permissions list <mailbox> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string  | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required) |
| `--include-inherited`     | boolean | Also show inherited permissions (inherited: true).     |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange permissions list shared-finance@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange permissions add`

Grant FullAccess, Send As or Send on Behalf on a mailbox **[destructive]**

full = open the mailbox (auto-mapped into Outlook unless --no-automap); sendas = send as the mailbox; sendonbehalf = send "on behalf of". Destructive because it opens a mailbox to someone. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange permissions add <mailbox> <user> --access <string> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string  | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required)                                 |
| `<user>` / `--user`       | string  | Who gets (or loses) access: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required)              |
| `--access`                | string  | full, sendas or sendonbehalf. (required; one of `full`, `sendas`, `sendonbehalf`)      |
| `--automap`               | boolean | FullAccess only: add to Outlook automatically (--no-automap to skip). (default `true`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange permissions add shared-finance@contoso.com bob@contoso.com --access full
tenantctl exchange permissions add jane@contoso.com bob@contoso.com --access sendas
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange permissions remove`

Revoke FullAccess, Send As or Send on Behalf on a mailbox **[destructive]**

Removes the permission; Outlook drops an auto-mapped mailbox within a few hours. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange permissions remove <mailbox> <user> --access <string>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required)                            |
| `<user>` / `--user`       | string | Who gets (or loses) access: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required)         |
| `--access`                | string | full, sendas or sendonbehalf. (required; one of `full`, `sendas`, `sendonbehalf`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange permissions remove shared-finance@contoso.com bob@contoso.com --access full
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange shared-mailbox create`

Create a shared mailbox and give members FullAccess + Send As **[write]**

New-Mailbox -Shared, then FullAccess (auto-mapped) and SendAs for each member, in one session. Shared mailboxes need no license up to 50 GB without archive or hold. A member grant can fail right after creation while Exchange replicates; retry it with `exchange permissions add`. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange shared-mailbox create --name <string> --email <string> [options]
```

| Argument    | Type     | Description                                     |
| ----------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `--name`    | string   | Display name (also the unique Name). (required) |
| `--email`   | string   | Primary SMTP address. (required)                |
| `--members` | string[] | Users who get FullAccess and SendAs.            |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange shared-mailbox create --name "Finance" --email finance@contoso.com --members jane@contoso.com,bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange mailbox convert`

Convert a mailbox between user (regular) and shared **[destructive]**

Typical leaver flow: convert to shared, grant access, then remove the license. A shared mailbox over 50 GB, with an archive, or on hold still needs a license; the preview shows size, archive and holds. Converting to regular needs a license on the account before it can be used. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange mailbox convert <mailbox> --to <string>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required) |
| `--to`                    | string | Target type. (required; one of `shared`, `regular`)    |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange mailbox convert jane@contoso.com --to shared
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange mailbox details`

Exchange-side mailbox facts: type, aliases, GAL visibility, forwarding, hold, archive, size, last logon

Get-Mailbox + Get-MailboxStatistics in one session. Complements `tenantctl exchange mailbox` (Graph settings). `statistics` is { error } when the mailbox was never logged on to. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange mailbox details <mailbox>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange mailbox details jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange dl list`

List distribution lists and mail-enabled security groups

--search matches name, alias and email (ambiguous name resolution). Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange dl list [options]
```

| Argument   | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--search` | string  | Name, alias or email prefix.                                 |
| `--top`    | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`    | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange dl list --search finance
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange dl members`

List members of a distribution list

Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange dl members <group> [options]
```

| Argument              | Type    | Description                                                                        |
| --------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<group>` / `--group` | string  | Distribution list or mail-enabled security group: email, alias or name. (required) |
| `--top`               | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                          |
| `--all`               | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                       |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange dl members finance@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange dl add-member`

Add people to a distribution list **[write]**

Adds each member in one session and reports per member (`skipped` when already a member). Works even when you are not a group owner (BypassSecurityGroupManagerCheck). Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange dl add-member <group> <members>
```

| Argument                  | Type     | Description                                                                        |
| ------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<group>` / `--group`     | string   | Distribution list or mail-enabled security group: email, alias or name. (required) |
| `<members>` / `--members` | string[] | Members to add (email, alias or name). (required)                                  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange dl add-member finance@contoso.com jane@contoso.com bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange dl remove-member`

Remove someone from a distribution list **[destructive]**

Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange dl remove-member <group> <member>
```

| Argument                | Type   | Description                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<group>` / `--group`   | string | Distribution list or mail-enabled security group: email, alias or name. (required) |
| `<member>` / `--member` | string | Member to remove. (required)                                                       |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange dl remove-member finance@contoso.com bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange dl create`

Create a distribution list **[write]**

Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange dl create --name <string> --email <string> [options]
```

| Argument    | Type     | Description                                     |
| ----------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `--name`    | string   | Unique name (also the display name). (required) |
| `--email`   | string   | Primary SMTP address. (required)                |
| `--members` | string[] | Initial members.                                |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange dl create --name "Finance Team" --email finance@contoso.com --members jane@contoso.com,bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange quarantine list`

List quarantined messages (spam, phish, malware, policy)

Use for "I never got mail from X". `identity` feeds `quarantine release|delete`. Admins see all users' quarantine with Security Administrator or the Quarantine Administrator role group; Security Reader / Global Reader can view. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange quarantine list [options]
```

| Argument      | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--recipient` | string  | Recipient address.                                                                                                                                         |
| `--sender`    | string  | Sender address.                                                                                                                                            |
| `--days`      | number  | Received in the last N days (quarantine keeps up to 30). (default `7`)                                                                                     |
| `--type`      | string  | Why it was quarantined. (one of `Bulk`, `DataLossPrevention`, `FileTypeBlock`, `HighConfPhish`, `Malware`, `Phish`, `Spam`, `SPOMalware`, `TransportRule`) |
| `--top`       | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                                                                  |
| `--all`       | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                                                               |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange quarantine list --recipient jane@contoso.com
tenantctl exchange quarantine list --sender billing@vendor.com --days 14 --type Phish
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Security Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange quarantine release`

Release a quarantined message to its recipients **[destructive]**

Default and --to-all release to every original recipient; --user releases to specific addresses. Only release what you have checked is safe: phish/malware reach the inbox. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange quarantine release <identity> [options]
```

| Argument                    | Type     | Description                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<identity>` / `--identity` | string   | Quarantine Identity (GUID1\GUID2) from `exchange quarantine list`. (required) |
| `--to-all`                  | boolean  | Release to all original recipients (default).                                 |
| `--user`                    | string[] | Release only to these addresses.                                              |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange quarantine release "c14401cf-...\4c2ca98e-..." --to-all
tenantctl exchange quarantine release "c14401cf-...\4c2ca98e-..." --user jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Security Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange quarantine delete`

Delete a quarantined message **[destructive]**

Removes it from quarantine; it can no longer be released. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange quarantine delete <identity>
```

| Argument                    | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<identity>` / `--identity` | string | Quarantine Identity (GUID1\GUID2) from `exchange quarantine list`. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange quarantine delete "c14401cf-...\4c2ca98e-..."
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Security Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange hold`

Turn litigation hold on or off for a mailbox **[destructive]**

Litigation hold keeps every item, including deleted and edited ones, for --duration-days (default unlimited). Needs Exchange Online Plan 2 (or an archiving add-on) on the mailbox. Turning it off lets retention delete held items. --note sets the retention comment users see in Outlook. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange hold <mailbox> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string  | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required) |
| `--on`                    | boolean | Place the mailbox on litigation hold.                  |
| `--off`                   | boolean | Remove litigation hold.                                |
| `--duration-days`         | number  | Keep items N days from receipt (default unlimited).    |
| `--note`                  | string  | Retention comment shown in Outlook.                    |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange hold jane@contoso.com --on --duration-days 2555 --note "Legal case 42"
tenantctl exchange hold jane@contoso.com --off
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange archive enable`

Enable the online archive for a mailbox **[write]**

Enable-Mailbox -Archive. The archive needs no extra license up to 50 GB on most business plans. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange archive enable <mailbox>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string | Mailbox: UPN, email, alias or display name. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange archive enable jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange transport-rules`

List mail flow (transport) rules in priority order

Mail-flow troubleshooting: rules that redirect, block, add disclaimers or change spam scoring. `mode` Audit/AuditAndNotify means the rule is only tested, not enforced. Runs through Exchange Online PowerShell: needs pwsh 7 and the ExchangeOnlineManagement module (3.1+).

```
tenantctl exchange transport-rules [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange transport-rules
```

Permissions: Exchange Online PowerShell (`Exchange.Manage` / `Exchange.ManageAsApp`); role Exchange Administrator

### `tenantctl exchange rooms list`

List meeting rooms with building, floor and capacity

Rooms come from Places (room mailboxes with location metadata set in Exchange). A room missing here has no Places entry; its mailbox still exists (`tenantctl exchange mailbox details <room>`).

```
tenantctl exchange rooms list [options]
```

| Argument     | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--building` | string  | Only rooms whose building contains this text.                |
| `--capacity` | number  | Only rooms that seat at least N people.                      |
| `--top`      | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`      | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange rooms list --building "HQ" --capacity 8
```

Permissions: delegated `Place.Read.All`; application `Place.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange rooms free`

Find meeting rooms free for a whole time window

Reads free/busy (getSchedule) for every matching room and returns those with nothing but free time in [start, end). `busy` lists rooms with tentative/busy/oof items; `unknown` lists rooms whose availability could not be read. Times without an offset are UTC.

```
tenantctl exchange rooms free --start <string> --end <string> [options]
```

| Argument     | Type   | Description                                   |
| ------------ | ------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `--start`    | string | Window start, ISO date-time. (required)       |
| `--end`      | string | Window end, ISO date-time. (required)         |
| `--building` | string | Only rooms whose building contains this text. |
| `--capacity` | number | Only rooms that seat at least N people.       |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange rooms free --start 2026-11-12T14:00:00Z --end 2026-11-12T15:00:00Z --capacity 6
```

Permissions: delegated `Place.Read.All`, `Calendars.ReadBasic`; application `Place.Read.All`, `Calendars.ReadBasic`

### `tenantctl exchange trace`

Message trace: did an email reach Exchange Online, and what happened to it

Start here for "my email didn't arrive". One row per recipient with status: delivered, failed, pending, quarantined, filteredAsSpam, expanded (sent to a group). Searches the last --days (default 2, max 10 per query) or an explicit --start/--end window within the last 90 days. --sender/--recipient are exact SMTP addresses; --subject matches a substring. Then run `tenantctl exchange trace details <id> --recipient <addr>` for the hop-by-hop events and failure reason. Prerequisite: the tenant needs the Microsoft message-trace service principal (appId 8bd644d1-64a1-4d4b-ae52-2e0cbf64e373; create it once with `New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId 8bd644d1-64a1-4d4b-ae52-2e0cbf64e373`). Throttled at 100 requests per 5 minutes.

```
tenantctl exchange trace [options]
```

| Argument      | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--sender`    | string  | Exact sender SMTP address.                                                                                                                       |
| `--recipient` | string  | Exact recipient SMTP address.                                                                                                                    |
| `--subject`   | string  | Text contained in the subject.                                                                                                                   |
| `--status`    | string  | Only messages with this delivery status. (one of `delivered`, `failed`, `pending`, `expanded`, `quarantined`, `filteredAsSpam`, `gettingStatus`) |
| `--days`      | number  | Search the last N days (max 10). (default `2`)                                                                                                   |
| `--start`     | string  | Window start, ISO (overrides --days).                                                                                                            |
| `--end`       | string  | Window end, ISO (default now).                                                                                                                   |
| `--top`       | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                                                        |
| `--all`       | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                                                     |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange trace --recipient jane@contoso.com --sender billing@vendor.com
tenantctl exchange trace --sender jane@contoso.com --status failed --days 7
tenantctl exchange trace --subject "Q3 report" --start 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-10-08T00:00:00Z
```

Permissions: delegated `ExchangeMessageTrace.Read.All`; application `ExchangeMessageTrace.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange trace details`

Delivery events for one traced message and recipient (why it failed or was filtered)

Answers "why didn't my email arrive": each event (Receive, Deliver, Fail, Spam/Malware detection, Transport rule, Defer...) with its action and description; the last event usually explains the outcome. traceId is the `id` from `tenantctl exchange trace`. --recipient is required for traces older than 48 hours or with several recipients. Prerequisite: the tenant needs the Microsoft message-trace service principal (appId 8bd644d1-64a1-4d4b-ae52-2e0cbf64e373; create it once with `New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId 8bd644d1-64a1-4d4b-ae52-2e0cbf64e373`). Throttled at 100 requests per 5 minutes.

```
tenantctl exchange trace details <trace-id> [options]
```

| Argument                    | Type   | Description                                   |
| --------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `<trace-id>` / `--trace-id` | string | Trace id from `exchange trace`. (required)    |
| `--recipient`               | string | Recipient SMTP address of the traced message. |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange trace details 4451a062-48cb-e80d-e8c0-196330437ae6 --recipient jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `ExchangeMessageTrace.Read.All`; application `ExchangeMessageTrace.Read.All`

### `tenantctl exchange usage`

Mailbox storage per user, quotas and percent used (usage report)

Answers "whose mailbox is full?". percentUsed is storage used against the Prohibit Send quota (the point where the user can no longer send); --near-quota keeps mailboxes at 90% or more. Sorted fullest first. Data comes from the Microsoft 365 usage report (refreshed daily, see reportRefreshDate). If the tenant hides user details in reports (Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Reports), names and UPNs are concealed hashes and --user cannot match. Delegated callers need a reports role such as Reports Reader.

```
tenantctl exchange usage [options]
```

| Argument       | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--user`       | string  | Only rows whose UPN or display name contains this text.      |
| `--near-quota` | boolean | Only mailboxes at 90% or more of the send quota.             |
| `--top`        | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`        | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl exchange usage --near-quota
tenantctl exchange usage --user jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Reports.Read.All`; application `Reports.Read.All`; role Reports Reader or Exchange Administrator or Global Reader

## sharepoint

Sites, libraries, files, sharing and permissions, OneDrive

### `tenantctl sharepoint sites list`

Find SharePoint sites by keyword, or list every site (app-only)

With --search, matches site titles/URLs (/sites?search=). Without it, app-only profiles list every site in the tenant (/sites/getAllSites, application permission only); delegated sign-ins must pass --search. OneDrive personal sites show isPersonalSite: true. Next: `sharepoint sites get <webUrl>`.

```
tenantctl sharepoint sites list [options]
```

| Argument   | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--search` | string  | Keyword matched against site name/title/URL.                 |
| `--top`    | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`    | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint sites list --search finance
tenantctl sharepoint sites list --all
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.Read.All`; application `Sites.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint sites get`

Show a site: storage quota, library count, and its Microsoft 365 group and owners

Answers "how full is this site", "who owns it", "is it a Teams/M365 group site". storage is the default document library quota (state normal/nearing <10% left/critical <1% left/exceeded). groupConnected is derived from the default library being owned by an M365 group; owners are that group's owners. Classic site collection admins are not exposed by Graph. Next: `sharepoint sites permissions`, `sites drives`.

```
tenantctl sharepoint sites get <site>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<site>` / `--site` | string | Site URL (any page or file URL under it works), Graph site id, or site name. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint sites get https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `Sites.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint sites drives`

List the document libraries of a site with their storage use

Each library (drive) with owner and quota. Libraries of one site share the site storage quota, so percentUsed is the same site-wide figure. Use a library id with `files` commands as driveId:itemId.

```
tenantctl sharepoint sites drives <site> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<site>` / `--site` | string  | Site URL (any page or file URL under it works), Graph site id, or site name. (required) |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                               |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                            |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint sites drives https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.Read.All`; application `Sites.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint sites permissions`

Show which apps have Sites.Selected access to a site, and its M365 group owner/member counts

appPermissions lists applications granted access to this specific site (Sites.Selected grants), with roles such as read or write. For group-connected sites, site access follows the Microsoft 365 group: owners are site owners, members are site members (counts shown; list them with `entra groups members`). Classic SharePoint groups (Owners/Members/Visitors), site collection admins and per-user site grants are not exposed by Graph v1.0; use SharePoint Online Management Shell or PnP PowerShell. To see who can open a particular file use `sharepoint files permissions`. Reading app grants needs Sites.FullControl.All.

```
tenantctl sharepoint sites permissions <site>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<site>` / `--site` | string | Site URL (any page or file URL under it works), Graph site id, or site name. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint sites permissions https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.FullControl.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`; application `Sites.FullControl.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint files search`

Find files by name or content in a site, or across SharePoint/OneDrive

With --site, searches that site's default library. Without it, uses Microsoft Search across all sites and OneDrives the caller can see (app-only: shared content in one geo region, --region or derived from the tenant). Use the returned driveId:id as <ref> for `files get`, `files permissions`, `files versions`.

```
tenantctl sharepoint files search <query> [options]
```

| Argument              | Type    | Description                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<query>` / `--query` | string  | Search text. (required)                                                      |
| `--site`              | string  | Site whose default library contains <ref> as a path, e.g. "Reports/Q1.xlsx". |
| `--region`            | string  | App-only tenant-wide search region (NAM, EUR, ...).                          |
| `--top`               | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                    |
| `--all`               | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                 |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint files search "budget 2026"
tenantctl sharepoint files search invoice --site finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.Read.All`; application `Sites.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint files get`

Show a file or folder: size, type, who created/changed it, and whether it is shared

sharedScope (anonymous/organization/users) appears when the item is shared. URLs are resolved through the /shares API, which needs Files.ReadWrite.All or Sites.ReadWrite.All even for reads; --site <site> with a path or driveId:itemId avoids that. Delegated sign-ins only see files the signed-in user can open (SharePoint Administrator does not grant file access); use app-only for tenant-wide. Next: `files permissions` for exactly who has access.

```
tenantctl sharepoint files get <ref> [options]
```

| Argument          | Type   | Description                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<ref>` / `--ref` | string | File/folder URL or sharing link, driveId:itemId, or a library path when --site is given. (required) |
| `--site`          | string | Site whose default library contains <ref> as a path, e.g. "Reports/Q1.xlsx".                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint files get "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/finance/EbC..."
tenantctl sharepoint files get "Reports/Q1.xlsx" --site finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.Read.All`; application `Sites.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint files permissions`

Who can access a file or folder: sharing links, direct grants, inherited access, externals

The answer to "who can see this file". kind: link (linkScope anonymous = anyone with the URL, no sign-in; organization = anyone in the tenant with the URL; users = only named people; existingAccess = no new access), direct (granted to a person/group), inherited (from a parent folder or the library; inheritedFrom shows where). grantedTo lists people/groups with email and external (outside the tenant's verified domains or a guest account). anonymousLinks and externalUsers summarize the risk. Permission ids feed `files unshare`. URLs are resolved through the /shares API, which needs Files.ReadWrite.All or Sites.ReadWrite.All even for reads; --site <site> with a path or driveId:itemId avoids that. Delegated sign-ins only see files the signed-in user can open (SharePoint Administrator does not grant file access); use app-only for tenant-wide.

```
tenantctl sharepoint files permissions <ref> [options]
```

| Argument          | Type   | Description                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<ref>` / `--ref` | string | File/folder URL or sharing link, driveId:itemId, or a library path when --site is given. (required) |
| `--site`          | string | Site whose default library contains <ref> as a path, e.g. "Reports/Q1.xlsx".                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint files permissions "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/hr/EfX..."
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.Read.All`, `Domain.Read.All`; application `Sites.Read.All`, `Domain.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint files unshare`

Remove a sharing link or direct grant from a file, or every sharing link with --all-links **[destructive]**

Removes access immediately: anyone relying on the link/grant loses it. Pass a permission id from `files permissions`, or --all-links to delete every non-inherited sharing link. Inherited permissions cannot be removed on the item; unshare them on the parent named in inheritedFrom. The preview lists exactly what will be removed. URLs are resolved through the /shares API, which needs Files.ReadWrite.All or Sites.ReadWrite.All even for reads; --site <site> with a path or driveId:itemId avoids that. Delegated sign-ins only see files the signed-in user can open (SharePoint Administrator does not grant file access); use app-only for tenant-wide.

```
tenantctl sharepoint files unshare <ref> [permission-id] [options]
```

| Argument                              | Type    | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<ref>` / `--ref`                     | string  | File/folder URL or sharing link, driveId:itemId, or a library path when --site is given. (required) |
| `<permission-id>` / `--permission-id` | string  | Permission id to remove.                                                                            |
| `--all-links`                         | boolean | Remove every sharing link on the item.                                                              |
| `--site`                              | string  | Site whose default library contains <ref> as a path, e.g. "Reports/Q1.xlsx".                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint files unshare "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/finance/EbC..." aTowIy5mfG1lbWJl
tenantctl sharepoint files unshare "Reports/Q1.xlsx" --site finance --all-links
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.ReadWrite.All`; application `Sites.ReadWrite.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint files versions`

List the version history of a file, newest first

Version ids feed `files restore-version`. The first entry (current: true) is the live version. URLs are resolved through the /shares API, which needs Files.ReadWrite.All or Sites.ReadWrite.All even for reads; --site <site> with a path or driveId:itemId avoids that. Delegated sign-ins only see files the signed-in user can open (SharePoint Administrator does not grant file access); use app-only for tenant-wide.

```
tenantctl sharepoint files versions <ref> [options]
```

| Argument          | Type    | Description                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<ref>` / `--ref` | string  | File/folder URL or sharing link, driveId:itemId, or a library path when --site is given. (required) |
| `--site`          | string  | Site whose default library contains <ref> as a path, e.g. "Reports/Q1.xlsx".                        |
| `--top`           | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                           |
| `--all`           | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint files versions "Reports/Q1.xlsx" --site finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.Read.All`; application `Sites.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint files restore-version`

Make an earlier version of a file the current version **[write]**

Restoring adds a new current version with the old content; history is kept, so it can be undone by restoring again. Get version ids from `files versions`. URLs are resolved through the /shares API, which needs Files.ReadWrite.All or Sites.ReadWrite.All even for reads; --site <site> with a path or driveId:itemId avoids that. Delegated sign-ins only see files the signed-in user can open (SharePoint Administrator does not grant file access); use app-only for tenant-wide.

```
tenantctl sharepoint files restore-version <ref> <version-id> [options]
```

| Argument                        | Type   | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<ref>` / `--ref`               | string | File/folder URL or sharing link, driveId:itemId, or a library path when --site is given. (required) |
| `<version-id>` / `--version-id` | string | Version id, e.g. 3.0. (required)                                                                    |
| `--site`                        | string | Site whose default library contains <ref> as a path, e.g. "Reports/Q1.xlsx".                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint files restore-version "Reports/Q1.xlsx" 3.0 --site finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Sites.ReadWrite.All`; application `Sites.ReadWrite.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint onedrive get`

Show a user's OneDrive: URL, storage used/remaining, quota state

Answers "is Jane's OneDrive full", "where is Bob's OneDrive". state: normal, nearing (<10% left), critical (<1% left), exceeded (uploads blocked). recycleBinGb counts toward usage. NOT_FOUND usually means the OneDrive was never provisioned (user never opened it) or the user has no SharePoint/OneDrive license. Next: `sharepoint onedrive usage --user <upn>` for file counts and last activity.

```
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive get <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                        |
| ------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | UPN, email, name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive get jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Files.Read.All`, `User.ReadBasic.All`; application `Files.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint onedrive usage`

OneDrive storage and activity per account from the usage report

Tenant-wide report: storage used/allocated, file counts and last activity per OneDrive. Use --near-quota to find accounts at 90%+ (sorted fullest first), --user for one person. For a live single-user view use `onedrive get`. Usage reports lag 24-48 hours. If the tenant conceals names in reports, owners and URLs appear hashed and filters cannot match them (turn it off in Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Reports). Delegated callers need a reports role such as Reports Reader.

```
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive usage [options]
```

| Argument       | Type    | Description                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--user`       | string  | Only this owner (UPN or display name).                                                        |
| `--near-quota` | boolean | Only accounts/sites using 90% or more of their allocated storage.                             |
| `--period`     | string  | Activity window the report aggregates over. (one of `D7`, `D30`, `D90`, `D180`; default `D7`) |
| `--top`        | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                     |
| `--all`        | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive usage --near-quota
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive usage --user jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Reports.Read.All`; application `Reports.Read.All`; role Reports Reader

### `tenantctl sharepoint sites usage`

SharePoint site storage, file counts and last activity from the usage report

Tenant-wide report sorted by storage used: find full sites (--near-quota), inactive sites (daysSinceActivity) or one site (--site, matched against the URL). Excludes OneDrive (see `onedrive usage`). Usage reports lag 24-48 hours. If the tenant conceals names in reports, owners and URLs appear hashed and filters cannot match them (turn it off in Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Reports). Delegated callers need a reports role such as Reports Reader.

```
tenantctl sharepoint sites usage [options]
```

| Argument       | Type    | Description                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--site`       | string  | Only sites whose URL contains this text.                                                      |
| `--near-quota` | boolean | Only accounts/sites using 90% or more of their allocated storage.                             |
| `--period`     | string  | Activity window the report aggregates over. (one of `D7`, `D30`, `D90`, `D180`; default `D7`) |
| `--top`        | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                     |
| `--all`        | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint sites usage --near-quota
tenantctl sharepoint sites usage --site /sites/finance
```

Permissions: delegated `Reports.Read.All`; application `Reports.Read.All`; role Reports Reader

### `tenantctl sharepoint onedrive grant`

Give someone access to another user's whole OneDrive (departing-employee handover) **[destructive]**

Shares the owner's OneDrive root folder, i.e. all of their files, with the grantee (sign-in required) and returns the drive URL to send them. It does NOT make the grantee a site collection admin of the OneDrive (for that use SharePoint admin center or `Set-SPOUser -IsSiteCollectionAdmin` / PnP): folders or files inside that have their own (broken-inheritance) permissions are not covered, and the grantee cannot manage OneDrive settings. The drive must still exist: a deleted user's OneDrive is retained only for the OneDrive retention period (30 days by default after deletion). --notify emails the grantee a sharing link; --expires-days is honoured by SharePoint only for that link-based invitation, so pair it with --notify. Undo with `onedrive revoke <owner> <grantee>`. Delegated callers can only change sharing on OneDrives they can already open (being SharePoint Administrator is not enough); use an app-only profile with Files.ReadWrite.All for handovers.

```
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive grant <owner> <grantee> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<owner>` / `--owner`     | string  | OneDrive owner: UPN, email, name or id. (required)                                       |
| `<grantee>` / `--grantee` | string  | Who gets access: UPN, email, name or id. (required)                                      |
| `--role`                  | string  | read = view/download; write = also edit/delete. (one of `read`, `write`; default `read`) |
| `--notify`                | boolean | Email the grantee a sharing invitation.                                                  |
| `--expires-days`          | number  | Access expires after N days (only with --notify).                                        |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive grant bob@contoso.com manager@contoso.com
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive grant bob@contoso.com manager@contoso.com --role write --notify --expires-days 30
```

Permissions: delegated `Files.ReadWrite.All`, `User.ReadBasic.All`; application `Files.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint onedrive revoke`

Remove someone's access to another user's OneDrive root (undo onedrive grant) **[destructive]**

Deletes the grantee's own permissions on the OneDrive root folder (direct grants and links only they hold). Links that also include other people are listed under `sharedLinks` and left alone; remove them with `files unshare`. Access the grantee has to individual files shared separately is not touched (see `files permissions`). Delegated callers can only change sharing on OneDrives they can already open (being SharePoint Administrator is not enough); use an app-only profile with Files.ReadWrite.All for handovers.

```
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive revoke <owner> <grantee>
```

| Argument                  | Type   | Description                                        |
| ------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `<owner>` / `--owner`     | string | OneDrive owner: UPN, email, name or id. (required) |
| `<grantee>` / `--grantee` | string | Whose access to remove. (required)                 |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint onedrive revoke bob@contoso.com manager@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Files.ReadWrite.All`, `User.ReadBasic.All`; application `Files.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl sharepoint settings`

Show tenant SharePoint/OneDrive settings: external sharing, domain lists, idle sign-out, sync

Answers "can people share externally", "are anonymous links allowed", "which domains can we share with". sharingCapability is the tenant-wide ceiling; individual sites can only be more restrictive (per-site sharing settings are not in Graph). Delegated callers need SharePoint Administrator or Global Reader. Change sharing with `sharepoint settings set --sharing`.

```
tenantctl sharepoint settings
```

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint settings
```

Permissions: delegated `SharePointTenantSettings.Read.All`; application `SharePointTenantSettings.Read.All`; role SharePoint Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl sharepoint settings set`

Change the tenant-wide external sharing level for SharePoint and OneDrive **[destructive]**

Tenant-wide and immediate. Lowering it disables existing links/guest access above the new level across every site and OneDrive (e.g. to existingExternalUserSharingOnly stops all anonymous links). Levels: disabled < existingExternalUserSharingOnly < externalUserSharingOnly < externalUserAndGuestSharing (anonymous links). Needs SharePoint Administrator in delegated mode.

```
tenantctl sharepoint settings set --sharing <string>
```

| Argument    | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--sharing` | string | New tenant sharing capability. (required; one of `disabled`, `existingExternalUserSharingOnly`, `externalUserSharingOnly`, `externalUserAndGuestSharing`) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl sharepoint settings set --sharing externalUserSharingOnly
```

Permissions: delegated `SharePointTenantSettings.ReadWrite.All`; application `SharePointTenantSettings.ReadWrite.All`; role SharePoint Administrator

## purview

Unified audit log search (who did what, across services), eDiscovery cases and holds

### `tenantctl purview audit search`

Search the unified audit log: who did what, when, from where, across Microsoft 365

Answers "who deleted this file", "who changed this mailbox", "what did Jane do yesterday". Combine --user (UPN of the person who acted), --operation (exact names such as FileDeleted, MailItemsAccessed, Set-Mailbox, Add member to group.), --record-type (exchangeAdmin, exchangeItem, sharePointFileOperation, oneDrive, azureActiveDirectory, ...), --object (full file URL or Exchange object name), --ip and --keyword (free text inside the workload-specific audit data, not operation names). Searches run asynchronously in Purview (typically 1-5 minutes). If the search outlives --wait-seconds the result is { queryId, status, next } and `next` fetches the records later; nothing is lost. Records are kept 180 days with Audit (Standard), one year for Entra/Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive with Audit (Premium). details holds the useful auditData fields (file/site for SharePoint and OneDrive, mailbox/folders/subjects for Exchange mailbox activity, cmdlet parameters for Exchange admin, targets for Entra); --full returns raw records including all auditData. Presets: `audit file-deleted`, `audit mailbox-access`, `audit admin-changes`.

```
tenantctl purview audit search [options]
```

| Argument         | Type     | Description                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--user`         | string[] | UPN(s) of the person who performed the activity.                                                               |
| `--operation`    | string[] | Operation name(s), e.g. FileDeleted, MailItemsAccessed.                                                        |
| `--record-type`  | string[] | Audit record type(s), e.g. exchangeAdmin, sharePointFileOperation.                                             |
| `--keyword`      | string   | Free text matched inside the workload-specific audit data.                                                     |
| `--object`       | string[] | Full file/folder URL (SharePoint/OneDrive) or object name (Exchange admin). Repeat the flag.                   |
| `--ip`           | string[] | Client IP address(es).                                                                                         |
| `--days`         | number   | Search the last N days (ignored when --start is given). (default `7`)                                          |
| `--start`        | string   | Window start (ISO date/time). Overrides --days.                                                                |
| `--end`          | string   | Window end (ISO date/time). Default: now.                                                                      |
| `--wait-seconds` | number   | How long to wait for the search; if it is still running, the query id is returned to re-check. (default `120`) |
| `--top`          | number   | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                      |
| `--all`          | boolean  | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview audit search --user jane@contoso.com --days 2
tenantctl purview audit search --operation FileDeleted --object "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/finance/Shared Documents/Q1.xlsx"
tenantctl purview audit search --operation Set-Mailbox,Add-MailboxPermission --days 30
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All`; application `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All`; role Audit Reader or Compliance Administrator

### `tenantctl purview audit results`

Status and records of an existing audit search

Use the queryId returned when `audit search` (or a preset) outlived its wait, or one listed by `audit queries`. Waits up to --wait-seconds if it is still running (0 = just check). details holds the useful auditData fields (file/site for SharePoint and OneDrive, mailbox/folders/subjects for Exchange mailbox activity, cmdlet parameters for Exchange admin, targets for Entra); --full returns raw records including all auditData.

```
tenantctl purview audit results <query-id> [options]
```

| Argument                    | Type    | Description                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<query-id>` / `--query-id` | string  | Audit query id. (required)                                                                                   |
| `--wait-seconds`            | number  | How long to wait for the search; if it is still running, the query id is returned to re-check. (default `0`) |
| `--top`                     | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                    |
| `--all`                     | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                 |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview audit results 168ec429-084b-a489-90d8-504a87846305
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All`; application `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All`; role Audit Reader or Compliance Administrator

### `tenantctl purview audit queries`

Recent audit searches with their status and filters

Lists audit log queries created in this tenant (by anyone using the API), so an earlier search can be re-read with `audit results <queryId>` instead of re-running it.

```
tenantctl purview audit queries [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview audit queries
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All`; application `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All`; role Audit Reader or Compliance Administrator

### `tenantctl purview audit file-deleted`

Who deleted files on a SharePoint site or OneDrive (including recycle bin purges)

Preset over `audit search` with operations FileDeleted, FileDeletedFirstStageRecycleBin, FileDeletedSecondStageRecycleBin, FolderDeleted, FolderDeletedFirstStageRecycleBin, FolderDeletedSecondStageRecycleBin. The site URL (and --file name) is sent as the keyword and records are then kept only when their site matches, so the result is exact. FirstStageRecycleBin = emptied from the site recycle bin; SecondStage = purged from the site collection recycle bin (unrecoverable after that). Searches run asynchronously in Purview (typically 1-5 minutes). If the search outlives --wait-seconds the result is { queryId, status, next } and `next` fetches the records later; nothing is lost. Records are kept 180 days with Audit (Standard), one year for Entra/Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive with Audit (Premium).

```
tenantctl purview audit file-deleted --site <string> [options]
```
