| Argument         | Type     | Description                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--site`         | string   | Site or OneDrive URL, or site name. (required)                                                                 |
| `--file`         | string   | Only files/folders with this name.                                                                             |
| `--user`         | string[] | Only deletions by these UPN(s).                                                                                |
| `--days`         | number   | Search the last N days (ignored when --start is given). (default `7`)                                          |
| `--start`        | string   | Window start (ISO date/time). Overrides --days.                                                                |
| `--end`          | string   | Window end (ISO date/time). Default: now.                                                                      |
| `--wait-seconds` | number   | How long to wait for the search; if it is still running, the query id is returned to re-check. (default `120`) |
| `--top`          | number   | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                      |
| `--all`          | boolean  | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview audit file-deleted --site https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/finance --file Q1.xlsx
tenantctl purview audit file-deleted --site https://contoso-my.sharepoint.com/personal/jane_contoso_com --days 30
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLogsQuery-SharePoint.Read.All`, `AuditLogsQuery-OneDrive.Read.All`, `Sites.Read.All`; application `AuditLogsQuery-SharePoint.Read.All`, `AuditLogsQuery-OneDrive.Read.All`, `Sites.Read.All`; role Audit Reader or Compliance Administrator

### `tenantctl purview audit mailbox-access`

Who opened, sent from or deleted items in a mailbox (owner, delegates, admins, apps)

Preset over `audit search` with mailbox audit operations MailItemsAccessed, FolderBind, SendAs, SendOnBehalf, MoveToDeletedItems, SoftDelete, HardDelete, UpdateInboxRules, UpdateFolderPermissions. Mailbox audit records are filed under the person who acted, so the mailbox owner is matched through the audit data (MailboxOwnerUPN), not --user. --accessed-by narrows to one actor; --non-owner hides the owner's own activity (the usual question after a compromise or a delegate dispute). details.logonType is owner, delegate or admin; MailItemsAccessed accessType is Bind (one item opened) or Sync (folder synced by a client). Searches run asynchronously in Purview (typically 1-5 minutes). If the search outlives --wait-seconds the result is { queryId, status, next } and `next` fetches the records later; nothing is lost. Records are kept 180 days with Audit (Standard), one year for Entra/Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive with Audit (Premium).

```
tenantctl purview audit mailbox-access <mailbox> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type     | Description                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<mailbox>` / `--mailbox` | string   | Mailbox owner: UPN, email, name or id. (required)                                                              |
| `--accessed-by`           | string[] | Only activity by these UPN(s).                                                                                 |
| `--non-owner`             | boolean  | Hide the mailbox owner's own activity.                                                                         |
| `--days`                  | number   | Search the last N days (ignored when --start is given). (default `7`)                                          |
| `--start`                 | string   | Window start (ISO date/time). Overrides --days.                                                                |
| `--end`                   | string   | Window end (ISO date/time). Default: now.                                                                      |
| `--wait-seconds`          | number   | How long to wait for the search; if it is still running, the query id is returned to re-check. (default `120`) |
| `--top`                   | number   | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                      |
| `--all`                   | boolean  | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview audit mailbox-access ceo@contoso.com --non-owner --days 14
tenantctl purview audit mailbox-access shared-finance@contoso.com --accessed-by bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLogsQuery-Exchange.Read.All`, `User.ReadBasic.All`; application `AuditLogsQuery-Exchange.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; role Audit Reader or Compliance Administrator

### `tenantctl purview audit admin-changes`

Recent Exchange admin cmdlets and Entra directory changes, optionally by one admin

Preset over `audit search` with record types exchangeAdmin, azureActiveDirectory: every Exchange admin cmdlet (Set-Mailbox, Add-MailboxPermission, New-TransportRule...) with its parameters, and Entra changes (users, groups, roles, apps). Answers "who changed this", "what did this admin do". Use --operation to narrow to specific cmdlets/activities. Searches run asynchronously in Purview (typically 1-5 minutes). If the search outlives --wait-seconds the result is { queryId, status, next } and `next` fetches the records later; nothing is lost. Records are kept 180 days with Audit (Standard), one year for Entra/Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive with Audit (Premium).

```
tenantctl purview audit admin-changes [options]
```

| Argument         | Type     | Description                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--user`         | string[] | Only changes by these admin UPN(s).                                                                            |
| `--operation`    | string[] | Only these cmdlets/activities.                                                                                 |
| `--days`         | number   | Search the last N days (ignored when --start is given). (default `7`)                                          |
| `--start`        | string   | Window start (ISO date/time). Overrides --days.                                                                |
| `--end`          | string   | Window end (ISO date/time). Default: now.                                                                      |
| `--wait-seconds` | number   | How long to wait for the search; if it is still running, the query id is returned to re-check. (default `120`) |
| `--top`          | number   | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                                      |
| `--all`          | boolean  | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                                   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview audit admin-changes --days 3
tenantctl purview audit admin-changes --user admin@contoso.com --operation Set-Mailbox
```

Permissions: delegated `AuditLogsQuery-Exchange.Read.All`, `AuditLogsQuery-Entra.Read.All`; application `AuditLogsQuery-Exchange.Read.All`, `AuditLogsQuery-Entra.Read.All`; role Audit Reader or Compliance Administrator

### `tenantctl purview ediscovery list`

List eDiscovery (Premium) cases with status

Cases the caller can see. Next: `ediscovery custodians <case>` for who is on hold. App-only use needs eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All plus the app's service principal added to the Purview eDiscoveryManager role group (and eDiscovery Administrator via Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin, or membership of each case). Delegated callers must be eDiscovery Manager/Administrator and a member of the case.

```
tenantctl purview ediscovery list [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                  |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview ediscovery list
```

Permissions: delegated `eDiscovery.Read.All`; application `eDiscovery.Read.All`; role eDiscovery Manager

### `tenantctl purview ediscovery create`

Create an eDiscovery (Premium) case **[write]**

Creates an empty case; add people with `ediscovery hold <case> <user...>`. App-only use needs eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All plus the app's service principal added to the Purview eDiscoveryManager role group (and eDiscovery Administrator via Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin, or membership of each case). Delegated callers must be eDiscovery Manager/Administrator and a member of the case.

```
tenantctl purview ediscovery create --name <string> [options]
```

| Argument        | Type   | Description                                  |
| --------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `--name`        | string | Case name (unique in the tenant). (required) |
| `--description` | string | Case description.                            |
| `--external-id` | string | Your own case/ticket number.                 |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview ediscovery create --name "HR-2026-014 Bob Smith" --description "Departure review"
```

Permissions: delegated `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All`; application `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All`; role eDiscovery Manager

### `tenantctl purview ediscovery custodians`

People in an eDiscovery case and whether their data is on hold

holdStatus: notApplied, applying, applied, removing, partial (some sources failed). status released = removed from the case. App-only use needs eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All plus the app's service principal added to the Purview eDiscoveryManager role group (and eDiscovery Administrator via Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin, or membership of each case). Delegated callers must be eDiscovery Manager/Administrator and a member of the case.

```
tenantctl purview ediscovery custodians <case>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                 |
| ------------------- | ------ | --------------------------- |
| `<case>` / `--case` | string | Case name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview ediscovery custodians "HR-2026-014"
```

Permissions: delegated `eDiscovery.Read.All`; application `eDiscovery.Read.All`; role eDiscovery Manager

### `tenantctl purview ediscovery hold`

Preserve people's mailbox and OneDrive under an eDiscovery case hold **[destructive]**

For each person: adds them as a custodian (if not already), attaches their mailbox and OneDrive as data sources, then applies the hold. Held content cannot be permanently deleted by the user or by retention until the hold is released, and it counts against their storage. Applying takes minutes to hours: check `ediscovery custodians <case>` until holdStatus is applied. App-only use needs eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All plus the app's service principal added to the Purview eDiscoveryManager role group (and eDiscovery Administrator via Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin, or membership of each case). Delegated callers must be eDiscovery Manager/Administrator and a member of the case.

```
tenantctl purview ediscovery hold <case> <user>
```

| Argument            | Type     | Description                                        |
| ------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `<case>` / `--case` | string   | Case name or id. (required)                        |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string[] | People to hold: UPN, email, name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview ediscovery hold "HR-2026-014" bob@contoso.com jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All`, `User.ReadBasic.All`; application `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; role eDiscovery Manager

### `tenantctl purview ediscovery release`

Remove the eDiscovery hold from a person's mailbox and OneDrive **[destructive]**

Calls removeHold for the custodian; they stay in the case (status active) so their data can still be searched, but held content becomes deletable again (retention policies and user deletes apply). Other cases or retention holds on the same person are unaffected. App-only use needs eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All plus the app's service principal added to the Purview eDiscoveryManager role group (and eDiscovery Administrator via Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin, or membership of each case). Delegated callers must be eDiscovery Manager/Administrator and a member of the case.

```
tenantctl purview ediscovery release <case> <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                   |
| ------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `<case>` / `--case` | string | Case name or id. (required)                   |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | Custodian: UPN, email, name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl purview ediscovery release "HR-2026-014" bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All`, `User.ReadBasic.All`; application `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; role eDiscovery Manager

## teams

Teams, channels, membership, presence, call quality

### `tenantctl teams list`

List teams in the tenant, optionally by name or archived state

Lists Microsoft 365 groups that have Teams enabled. --search matches words in the display name. --archived reads each team to find read-only (archived) ones, so it is slower on large tenants. Next: `tenantctl teams get <team>` for settings, owners and counts.

```
tenantctl teams list [options]
```

| Argument     | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--search`   | string  | Words in the team display name.                              |
| `--archived` | boolean | Only archived (read-only) teams.                             |
| `--top`      | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`      | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams list --search marketing
tenantctl teams list --archived --all
```

Permissions: delegated `Group.ReadBasic.All`, `Team.ReadBasic.All`; application `Group.ReadBasic.All`, `Team.ReadBasic.All`

### `tenantctl teams get`

Show a team: archived state, key settings, owners, member/guest/channel counts, link

Use to answer "who owns this team", "can guests/members create channels", "is it archived". `settings` keeps only the member, guest and messaging switches that admins are usually asked about. Sections that fail (missing permission) show `{ error }` instead of failing the whole view.

```
tenantctl teams get <team>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team` | string | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams get "Project Falcon"
```

Permissions: delegated `TeamSettings.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`, `Channel.ReadBasic.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; application `TeamSettings.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`, `Channel.ReadBasic.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; role Teams Administrator

### `tenantctl teams members`

List the owners, members and guests of a team

`role` is owner, member or guest. `membershipId` is the team membership (not the user id). Next: `tenantctl teams members add|remove <team> <user>`.

```
tenantctl teams members <team> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team` | string  | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |
| `--role`            | string  | Only this role. (one of `owner`, `member`, `guest`)                                             |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                       |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                    |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams members "Project Falcon" --role owner
```

Permissions: delegated `TeamMember.Read.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; application `TeamMember.Read.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`

### `tenantctl teams members add`

Add a user to a team as member or owner **[write]**

Adds the user directly to the team (and its Microsoft 365 group). --owner makes them an owner. Guests can be added only with delegated sign-in; app-only adds of guests are not supported by Graph.

```
tenantctl teams members add <team> <user> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team` | string  | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string  | User UPN, email, display name or id. (required)                                                 |
| `--owner`           | boolean | Add as an owner.                                                                                |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams members add "Project Falcon" jane@contoso.com
tenantctl teams members add Sales bob --owner
```

Permissions: delegated `TeamMember.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `TeamMember.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams members remove`

Remove a user from a team **[destructive]**

Removes the team membership (and the Microsoft 365 group membership), so the user loses access to the team's channels and files. A team's last owner cannot be removed.

```
tenantctl teams members remove <team> <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team` | string | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name or id. (required)                                                 |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams members remove "Project Falcon" jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `TeamMember.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `TeamMember.ReadWrite.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams channels`

List a team's channels with their type (standard, private, shared)

Private and shared channels have their own membership: use `tenantctl teams channels members <team> <channel>` when someone can see the team but not a channel.

```
tenantctl teams channels <team> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team` | string  | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                       |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                    |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams channels "Project Falcon"
```

Permissions: delegated `Channel.ReadBasic.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; application `Channel.ReadBasic.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`

### `tenantctl teams channels members`

List who is in a private or shared channel

Standard channels inherit team membership, so use `tenantctl teams members` for them. Shared channels can include people from other teams or tenants (tenantId differs).

```
tenantctl teams channels members <team> <channel> [options]
```

| Argument                  | Type    | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team`       | string  | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |
| `<channel>` / `--channel` | string  | Channel name or id (19:...). (required)                                                         |
| `--top`                   | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                       |
| `--all`                   | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                    |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams channels members "Project Falcon" "Leadership"
```

Permissions: delegated `ChannelMember.Read.All`, `Channel.ReadBasic.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; application `ChannelMember.Read.All`, `Channel.ReadBasic.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`

### `tenantctl teams user`

List the teams a user belongs to

Answers "which teams is X in". Covers direct team membership only; access through a shared channel does not appear here.

```
tenantctl teams user <user>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                     |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `<user>` / `--user` | string | User UPN, email, display name or id. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams user jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Team.ReadBasic.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `Team.ReadBasic.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams presence`

Show users' Teams presence (availability, activity, status message, out of office)

availability is the coloured dot (Available, Busy, DoNotDisturb, Away, Offline...); activity adds detail (InACall, InAMeeting, Presenting...). Useful before calling someone or when a user reports their status is stuck. Accepts several users at once.

```
tenantctl teams presence <users>
```

| Argument              | Type     | Description                                            |
| --------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<users>` / `--users` | string[] | One or more users (UPN, email, name or id). (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams presence jane@contoso.com bob@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Presence.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`; application `Presence.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams create`

Create a new team from the standard template **[write]**

Creates the Microsoft 365 group and team together. Graph accepts the request and provisions the team in the background, which can take several minutes. The result has the new teamId and operationId; `next` polls the operation (status succeeded/failed, wait 30+ seconds between checks). With app-only auth --owner is required (Graph needs an owner); with delegated sign-in the caller becomes an owner and --owner adds another.

```
tenantctl teams create --name <string> [options]
```

| Argument        | Type   | Description                                                            |
| --------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--name`        | string | Team display name. (required)                                          |
| `--description` | string | Team description.                                                      |
| `--visibility`  | string | Who can find and join. (one of `private`, `public`; default `private`) |
| `--owner`       | string | Owner (UPN, email, name or id). Required with app-only auth.           |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams create --name "Project Falcon" --description "Falcon launch" --owner jane@contoso.com
```

Permissions: delegated `Team.Create`, `User.Read.All`; application `Team.Create`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams archive`

Archive a team (make it read-only) **[destructive]**

Members can still read but no longer post, and the team moves to the archived list. Reversible with `tenantctl teams unarchive`. --spo-read-only also makes the SharePoint site read-only for members (delegated sign-in only).

```
tenantctl teams archive <team> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team` | string  | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |
| `--spo-read-only`   | boolean | Also make the team SharePoint site read-only for members.                                       |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams archive "Project Falcon"
```

Permissions: delegated `TeamSettings.ReadWrite.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; application `TeamSettings.ReadWrite.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; role Teams Administrator

### `tenantctl teams unarchive`

Restore an archived team to read-write **[write]**

```
tenantctl teams unarchive <team>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<team>` / `--team` | string | Team display name, group id, group mail address or a Teams link containing groupId=. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams unarchive "Project Falcon"
```

Permissions: delegated `TeamSettings.ReadWrite.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; application `TeamSettings.ReadWrite.All`, `Group.ReadBasic.All`; role Teams Administrator

### `tenantctl teams calls list`

List recent Teams calls and meetings (call records)

Call records appear about 15 minutes to a few hours after a call ends and are kept 30 days. --user limits to calls that user took part in. Needs app-only auth (application permission CallRecords.Read.All); delegated sign-in cannot read call records. Next: `tenantctl teams calls get <id>` for per-participant quality.

```
tenantctl teams calls list [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--days` | number  | Calls that started in the last N days (max 30). (default `1`) |
| `--user` | string  | Only calls this user joined (UPN, email, name or id).         |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                     |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams calls list --user jane@contoso.com --days 2
```

Permissions: application `CallRecords.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams calls get`

Diagnose one call: per-participant audio/video quality, network and failures

For "my Teams call was choppy/dropped". `quality` has one row per person: verdict poor|ok, the worst packet loss (0-1), jitter and round trip (ms), poor stream count with reasons, connection type (wifi/wired) and weakest Wi-Fi signal. A stream is poor by Call Quality Dashboard rules: packet loss > 10%, jitter > 30 ms, round trip > 500 ms, degradation > 1.0 or concealed samples > 7%. networkEventRatios are the fraction of the call the client saw bad network; high `receivedQuality` or `delay` with connection wifi usually points at the user's Wi-Fi. `failures` lists setup/midcall failures. Needs app-only auth (CallRecords.Read.All).

```
tenantctl teams calls get <id>
```

| Argument        | Type   | Description                                        |
| --------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `<id>` / `--id` | string | Call record id from `teams calls list`. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams calls get 2f1a6c87-...
```

Permissions: application `CallRecords.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams calls pstn`

List phone (PSTN) calls made or received through Teams Phone

Covers Microsoft Calling Plans and Operator Connect calls (not Direct Routing). Shows who called which number, duration in seconds and cost. Max range 90 days. Needs app-only auth (CallRecords.Read.All).

```
tenantctl teams calls pstn [options]
```

| Argument | Type    | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--days` | number  | Calls that started in the last N days (max 90). (default `7`) |
| `--top`  | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                     |
| `--all`  | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).  |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams calls pstn --days 7
```

Permissions: application `CallRecords.Read.All`

### `tenantctl teams activity`

Teams usage per user: last activity, chats, calls, meetings

From the Microsoft 365 usage report, which lags about 2 days. Use to check whether someone actually uses Teams. If the tenant conceals user details in reports (Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Reports), names and UPNs are replaced by hashes and --user cannot match. Delegated callers need a reports role such as Reports Reader.

```
tenantctl teams activity [options]
```

| Argument   | Type    | Description                                                      |
| ---------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--user`   | string  | Only this user (UPN, email, name or id).                         |
| `--period` | string  | Report window. (one of `D7`, `D30`, `D90`, `D180`; default `D7`) |
| `--top`    | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                        |
| `--all`    | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).     |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl teams activity --user jane@contoso.com
tenantctl teams activity --period D30 --top 20
```

Permissions: delegated `Reports.Read.All`; application `Reports.Read.All`; role Reports Reader or Teams Administrator or Teams Communications Administrator

## health

Microsoft 365 service health and message center

### `tenantctl health overview`

Current health of every Microsoft 365 service the tenant uses

First check when several users report the same problem ("Outlook is down", "Teams calls failing"). `degraded` lists services with an ongoing issue; `recentlyRestored` were fixed but not yet back to operational. Next: `tenantctl health issues --service "<service>" --active` for details.

```
tenantctl health overview
```

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl health overview
```

Permissions: delegated `ServiceHealth.Read.All`; application `ServiceHealth.Read.All`; role Service Support Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl health issues`

List service health incidents and advisories

incident = significant user impact; advisory = limited impact or a subset of users. --active hides resolved ones. --service takes the name shown by `tenantctl health overview` (e.g. "Exchange Online", "Microsoft Teams"). --days counts by last update. Next: `tenantctl health issue <id>` for the timeline.

```
tenantctl health issues [options]
```

| Argument           | Type    | Description                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--service`        | string  | Service name, e.g. "Exchange Online".                        |
| `--active`         | boolean | Only unresolved issues.                                      |
| `--days`           | number  | Only issues updated in the last N days.                      |
| `--classification` | string  | Incident or advisory. (one of `incident`, `advisory`)        |
| `--top`            | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                    |
| `--all`            | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow). |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl health issues --active
tenantctl health issues --service "Microsoft Teams" --days 7
```

Permissions: delegated `ServiceHealth.Read.All`; application `ServiceHealth.Read.All`; role Service Support Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl health issue`

Show one service health issue with its update timeline as plain text

`posts` are Microsoft's updates, newest first, with HTML removed. The latest post usually has the current status, scope of impact and next update time.

```
tenantctl health issue <id>
```

| Argument        | Type   | Description                                     |
| --------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `<id>` / `--id` | string | Issue id, e.g. EX123456 or TM654321. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl health issue EX123456
```

Permissions: delegated `ServiceHealth.Read.All`; application `ServiceHealth.Read.All`; role Service Support Administrator or Global Reader

### `tenantctl health messages`

List message center posts (upcoming changes, retirements, required actions)

Use for "what is changing in Teams/Exchange", "what do we need to act on". --action-required keeps posts with a deadline; --major keeps major changes (30 days notice). --days counts by last update. Categories: preventOrFixIssue, planForChange, stayInformed. Next: `tenantctl health message <id>`.

```
tenantctl health messages [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--service`         | string  | Service name, e.g. "Microsoft Teams".                                           |
| `--days`            | number  | Only posts updated in the last N days.                                          |
| `--major`           | boolean | Only major changes.                                                             |
| `--category`        | string  | Message category. (one of `preventOrFixIssue`, `planForChange`, `stayInformed`) |
| `--action-required` | boolean | Only posts with an action-required-by date.                                     |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                       |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                    |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl health messages --action-required
tenantctl health messages --service "Microsoft Teams" --days 30 --major
```

Permissions: delegated `ServiceMessage.Read.All`; application `ServiceMessage.Read.All`; role Message Center Reader or Global Reader

### `tenantctl health message`

Show one message center post with its body as plain text

```
tenantctl health message <id>
```

| Argument        | Type   | Description                           |
| --------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `<id>` / `--id` | string | Message id, e.g. MC123456. (required) |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl health message MC123456
```

Permissions: delegated `ServiceMessage.Read.All`; application `ServiceMessage.Read.All`; role Message Center Reader or Global Reader

## graph

Raw Microsoft Graph requests (escape hatch)

### `tenantctl graph get`

Raw GET of any Graph path; collections are paged like list commands

Use when no dedicated command covers what you need. Results come back unshaped. Needs whatever permission the endpoint documents.

```
tenantctl graph get <path> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<path>` / `--path` | string  | Graph path after the version, with any query string, e.g. "/users?$select=id,displayName". (required) |
| `--beta`            | boolean | Call the beta endpoint instead of v1.0.                                                               |
| `--advanced`        | boolean | Send ConsistencyLevel: eventual ($search, $count and advanced filters on directory objects).          |
| `--top`             | number  | Maximum results to return. (default `50`)                                                             |
| `--all`             | boolean | Return every result (pages through everything; can be slow).                                          |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl graph get "/users?$filter=department eq 'Sales'&$select=displayName,mail"
tenantctl graph get /deviceManagement/managedDevices --beta --top 5
```

### `tenantctl graph post`

Raw POST to any Graph path **[destructive]**

Escape hatch for operations no dedicated command covers. Always treated as destructive: it shows the request for approval before sending it. Prefer a dedicated command when one exists.

```
tenantctl graph post <path> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<path>` / `--path` | string  | Graph path after the version, with any query string, e.g. "/users?$select=id,displayName". (required) |
| `--body`            | string  | JSON request body.                                                                                    |
| `--beta`            | boolean | Call the beta endpoint instead of v1.0.                                                               |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl graph post /users/jane@contoso.com --body '{"jobTitle":"Manager"}'
```

### `tenantctl graph patch`

Raw PATCH to any Graph path **[destructive]**

Escape hatch for operations no dedicated command covers. Always treated as destructive: it shows the request for approval before sending it. Prefer a dedicated command when one exists.

```
tenantctl graph patch <path> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<path>` / `--path` | string  | Graph path after the version, with any query string, e.g. "/users?$select=id,displayName". (required) |
| `--body`            | string  | JSON request body.                                                                                    |
| `--beta`            | boolean | Call the beta endpoint instead of v1.0.                                                               |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl graph patch /users/jane@contoso.com --body '{"jobTitle":"Manager"}'
```

### `tenantctl graph put`

Raw PUT to any Graph path **[destructive]**

Escape hatch for operations no dedicated command covers. Always treated as destructive: it shows the request for approval before sending it. Prefer a dedicated command when one exists.

```
tenantctl graph put <path> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<path>` / `--path` | string  | Graph path after the version, with any query string, e.g. "/users?$select=id,displayName". (required) |
| `--body`            | string  | JSON request body.                                                                                    |
| `--beta`            | boolean | Call the beta endpoint instead of v1.0.                                                               |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl graph put /users/jane@contoso.com --body '{"jobTitle":"Manager"}'
```

### `tenantctl graph delete`

Raw DELETE to any Graph path **[destructive]**

Escape hatch for operations no dedicated command covers. Always treated as destructive: it shows the request for approval before sending it. Prefer a dedicated command when one exists.

```
tenantctl graph delete <path> [options]
```

| Argument            | Type    | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<path>` / `--path` | string  | Graph path after the version, with any query string, e.g. "/users?$select=id,displayName". (required) |
| `--body`            | string  | JSON request body.                                                                                    |
| `--beta`            | boolean | Call the beta endpoint instead of v1.0.                                                               |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl graph delete /users/jane@contoso.com
```

## auth

Sign in, sign out, show the current identity and permissions

### `tenantctl auth login`

Sign in (device code for delegated profiles; verifies credentials for app-only profiles)

Delegated: prints a code and URL on stderr; the user opens the URL, enters the code and signs in with an admin account. The command waits until they finish. Relay the stderr message to the user verbatim. By default it requests every read permission the CLI uses (plus write permissions when writes are enabled or --include-writes is passed). Without a profile it uses the Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools app, so no app registration is needed.

```
tenantctl auth login [options]
```

| Argument           | Type     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--service`        | string   | What to sign in to: graph (everything except the items below), exchange (Exchange admin commands that run through PowerShell), defender (Defender for Endpoint device actions). (one of `graph`, `exchange`, `defender`; default `graph`) |
| `--scopes`         | string[] | Graph only: request exactly these delegated scopes instead of the default set.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--include-writes` | boolean  | Graph only: also request the scopes write commands need.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--tenant`         | string   | Tenant id or domain to sign in to (default: the account's home tenant).                                                                                                                                                                   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl auth login
tenantctl auth login --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com --include-writes
```

### `tenantctl auth status`

Show who is signed in, the tenant, admin roles, granted permissions and whether writes are enabled

Run this first when a command fails with AUTH_* or FORBIDDEN, to see what the token actually grants.

```
tenantctl auth status
```

### `tenantctl auth logout`

Delete the cached tokens for the profile

```
tenantctl auth logout
```

## config

Profiles, settings, local audit log

### `tenantctl config init`

Create or update a profile (tenant, app registration, auth mode)

Delegated profiles need nothing else; `tenantctl auth login` works without this. App-only profiles need a tenant, the app registration client id, and either --cert (PEM with private key and certificate) or the TENANTCTL_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable. Secrets are never written to the config file.

```
tenantctl config init [options]
```

| Argument       | Type    | Description                                                         |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mode`       | string  | Auth mode (default: delegated). (one of `delegated`, `app`)         |
| `--tenant`     | string  | Tenant id or primary domain.                                        |
| `--client-id`  | string  | App registration (client) id.                                       |
| `--cert`       | string  | App-only: path to a PEM containing the private key and certificate. |
| `--thumbprint` | string  | App-only: SHA-256 thumbprint, if the PEM has no certificate.        |
| `--default`    | boolean | Make this the default profile.                                      |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl config init --mode app --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com --client-id 00000000-... --cert ~/certs/tenantctl.pem
tenantctl --profile fabrikam config init --tenant fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com
```

### `tenantctl config show`

Show the active profile with environment overrides applied (never shows secrets)

```
tenantctl config show
```

### `tenantctl config set`

Set one profile setting

```
tenantctl config set <key> <value>
```

| Argument              | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<key>` / `--key`     | string | Setting name. (required; one of `authMode`, `tenantId`, `clientId`, `certificatePath`, `certificateThumbprint`, `allowWrites`, `confirmMode`, `graphUrl`, `authorityHost`) |
| `<value>` / `--value` | string | New value. (required)                                                                                                                                                      |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl config set allowWrites true
tenantctl config set tenantId contoso.onmicrosoft.com
```

### `tenantctl config unset`

Remove one profile setting

```
tenantctl config unset <key>
```

| Argument          | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<key>` / `--key` | string | Setting name. (required; one of `authMode`, `tenantId`, `clientId`, `certificatePath`, `certificateThumbprint`, `allowWrites`, `confirmMode`, `graphUrl`, `authorityHost`) |

### `tenantctl config use`

Make a profile the default

```
tenantctl config use <name>
```

| Argument            | Type   | Description              |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------ |
| `<name>` / `--name` | string | Profile name. (required) |

### `tenantctl config audit-log`

Show the local log of write attempts made with this CLI (newest first)

```
tenantctl config audit-log [options]
```

| Argument | Type   | Description                     |
| -------- | ------ | ------------------------------- |
| `--top`  | number | Entries to show. (default `20`) |

## tools

Machine-readable catalog of every command (for agents)

### `tenantctl tools`

Machine-readable catalog of commands: arguments (JSON Schema), risk, permissions

Write commands are omitted unless writes are enabled or --include-writes is passed. Each entry has the exact argv prefix in `command`; pass args as --kebab-case flags.

```
tenantctl tools [domain] [options]
```

| Argument                | Type    | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `<domain>` / `--domain` | string  | Only this area.                                       |
| `--include-writes`      | boolean | Include write commands even when writes are disabled. |

## permissions

Graph permissions the app registration needs

### `tenantctl permissions`

List the Graph permissions to grant the app registration (or consent to) for this CLI

```
tenantctl permissions [options]
```

| Argument           | Type    | Description                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mode`           | string  | Permission type. (one of `delegated`, `application`; default `application`) |
| `--include-writes` | boolean | Include permissions for write commands.                                     |
| `--domain`         | string  | Only this area.                                                             |
| `--by-command`     | boolean | Show which commands need each permission.                                   |

Examples:

```sh
tenantctl permissions --mode application
tenantctl permissions --mode delegated --include-writes --by-command
```
